[Upload Example](#id76)[](#upload-example)
This operation allows manual upload of a local file to the [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault).
Note
When running the [execute](#weaver-execute) operation, any detected local file reference will be automatically uploaded
as [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) file in order to make it available for the remote Weaver server for [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) execution.
See also
[File Vault Inputs](processes.html#file-vault-inputs) and [Uploading File to the Vault](processes.html#vault-upload) provide more details about this feature.
weaver upload -u ${WEAVER_URL} -f /path/to/file.txt
client.upload("/path/to/file.txt")
Sample Output:
{
"description": "File successfully uploaded to vault.",
"access_token": "<ACCESS_TOKEN>",
"file_id": "e337a830-dbd6-4915-90ef-bfd46e237a3e",
"file_href": "vault://e337a830-dbd6-4915-90ef-bfd46e237a3e"
}

Processes[](#id1)
[Type of Processes](#id106)[](#type-of-processes)
Weaver supports multiple type of processes, as listed below. Each one of them are accessible through the same API interface, but they have different implications.
- [OGC API - Processes](#proc-ogc-api)(formerly known as- [WPS-REST](appendix.html#term-WPS-REST),- [WPS-T](appendix.html#term-WPS-T)or WPS-3)
See also
Section [Examples](examples.rst) provides multiple concrete use cases of [Deploy](#proc-op-deploy)
and [Execute](#proc-op-execute) request payloads for diverse set of applications.
[Builtin](#id107)[](#builtin)
These processes come pre-packaged with Weaver. They will be available directly on startup of the application and re-updated on each boot to make sure internal database references are updated with any source code changes.
Theses processes typically correspond to utility operations. They are specifically useful when employed as
step within a [Workflow](#workflow) process that requires data-type conversion between input/output of similar, but not
perfectly, compatible definitions.
As of the latest release, following builtin processes are available:
- weaver.processes.builtin.collection_processor- Implements parsing capabilities to support - [Collection Input](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/21-009.html#section_collection_input)as defined by the- [OGC API - Processes - Part 3: Workflows](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/21-009.html)extension. This allows- [Process Execution](#proc-op-execute)to employ- [Collection Inputs](#proc-col-inputs)in certain cases when conditions are met.
- weaver.processes.builtin.echo_process- Corresponds to the - [OGC API - Processes - Part 1: Core - Echo Process](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opengeospatial/ogcapi-processes/master/core/examples/json/ProcessDescription.json)definition. This- [Process](appendix.html#term-Process)is used to evaluate the- [API](appendix.html#term-API)against the OGC Execution Test Suite (ETS) for the- [Weaver Product Implementation](https://portal.ogc.org/public_ogc/compliance/product.php?pid=1825). It also is employed to test the implementation against a wide range of input and output formats.
- weaver.processes.builtin.file2string_array- Transforms a - [File Reference](#file-ref-types)input into- [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON)file containing an array of file references as value. This is typically employed to resolve a- [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON)array containing multiple sub-file references, allowing to “unpack” a single item into multiple references.
- weaver.processes.builtin.file_index_selector- Selects the single - [File Reference](#file-ref-types)at the provided index within an array of file- [URL](appendix.html#term-URL).
- weaver.processes.builtin.jsonarray2netcdf- Takes a single input - [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON)file which its content contains an array-list of NetCDF file references, and returns them directly as the corresponding list of output files. These two different file formats (single- [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON)to multiple NetCDF) can then be used to map two processes with these respective output and inputs.
- weaver.processes.builtin.metalink2netcdf- Extracts and fetches NetCDF files from a Metalink file containing an URL, and outputs the NetCDF file at a given index of the list.
All builtin processes are marked with [ weaver.processes.constants.CWL_REQUIREMENT_APP_BUILTIN](autoapi/weaver/processes/constants/index.html#weaver.processes.constants.CWL_REQUIREMENT_APP_BUILTIN) in the
[CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL)
hints section and are all defined in [. For explicit schema validation using the](autoapi/weaver/processes/builtin/index.html#module-weaver.processes.builtin)
weaver.processes.builtin[CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL)
requirements, the weaver:BuiltinRequirement can also be used.[WPS-1/2](#id108)[](#wps-1-2)
This kind of [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) corresponds to a traditional [WPS](appendix.html#term-WPS) [XML](appendix.html#term-XML) or [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON) endpoint
(depending of supported version) prior to [OGC API - Processes (WPS-REST, WPS-T, WPS-3)](#proc-wps-rest) specification. When an [OGC API - Processes](https://github.com/opengeospatial/ogcapi-processes) description is
deployed in Weaver using an URL reference to an WPS-1/2 process through the use of a [Remote Applications](package.html#app-pkg-wps1) requirement,
Weaver parses and converts the [XML](appendix.html#term-XML) or [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON) body of the [WPS](appendix.html#term-WPS) response and registers the process
locally. This allows a remote server offering limited functionalities (e.g.: no REST or OGC API bindings supported)
to provide them through Weaver.
A minimal [Deploy](#proc-op-deploy) request body for this kind of process could be as follows:
{
"processDescription": {
"process": {
"id": "my-process-reference"
}
},
"executionUnit": [
{
"href": "https://example.com/wps?service=WPS&request=DescribeProcess&identifier=my-process&version=1.0.0"
}
]
}
This would tell Weaver to locally [Deploy](#proc-op-deploy) the my-process-reference process using the WPS-1
URL reference that is expected to return a DescribeProcess [XML](appendix.html#term-XML) schema. Provided that this endpoint can be
resolved and parsed according to typical [WPS](appendix.html#term-WPS) specification, this should result into a successful [Process](appendix.html#term-Process)
registration.
The deployed [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) would then be accessible with [DescribeProcess](#proc-op-describe) requests.
The above deployment procedure can be automated on startup using Weaver’s wps_processes.yml configuration file.
Please refer to [Configuration of WPS Processes](configuration.html#configuration-of-wps-processes) section for more details on this matter.
Warning
Because Weaver creates a snapshot of the reference process at the moment it was deployed, the local process
definition could become out-of-sync with the remote reference where the [Execute](#proc-op-execute) request
will be sent. Refer to [Remote Provider](#remote-provider) section for more details to work around this issue.
Any [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) deployed from a [WPS](appendix.html#term-WPS) reference should have a resulting [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL) definition that either
contains WPS1Requirement in the hints section, or weaver:WPS1Requirement in the requirements section.
See also
[OGC API - Processes (WPS-REST, WPS-T, WPS-3)](#id109)[](#ogc-api-processes-wps-rest-wps-t-wps-3)
This [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) type is the main component of Weaver. All other types are converted to this one either
through some parsing (e.g.: [WPS-1/2](#proc-wps-12)) or with some requirement indicators
(e.g.: [Builtin](#proc-builtin), [Workflow](#proc-workflow)) for
special handling. The represented [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) is aligned with [OGC API - Processes](https://github.com/opengeospatial/ogcapi-processes) specifications.
When deploying one such [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) directly, it is expected to have a definition specified
with a [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL) [application-package](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/package.html#application-package), which provides resources about one of the described [Typical CWL Package Definition](package.html#app-pkg-types).
This is most of the time employed to wrap operations packaged in a reference [Docker](appendix.html#term-Docker) image, but it can also
wrap [Remote Applications](package.html#app-pkg-remote) to be executed on another server (i.e.: [ADES](appendix.html#term-ADES)). When the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) should be
deployed using a remote URL reference pointing at an existing [OGC API - Processes](https://github.com/opengeospatial/ogcapi-processes) description, the [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL) should
contain either OGCAPIRequirement in the hints section, or weaver:OGCAPIRequirement in the requirements
section.
The referenced [Application Package](appendix.html#term-Application-Package) can be provided in multiple ways as presented below.
Note
When a process is deployed with any of the below supported [Application Package](appendix.html#term-Application-Package) formats, additional parsing
of this [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL) as well as complementary details directly within the [WPS](appendix.html#term-WPS) deployment body is
accomplished. See [Correspondence between CWL and WPS fields](package.html#cwl-wps-mapping) section for more details.
[Package as Literal Execution Unit Block](#id110)[](#package-as-literal-execution-unit-block)
In this situation, the [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL) definition is provided as is using [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON)-formatted package embedded within the
[ POST {WEAVER_URL}/processes (Deploy)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Processes%2Fpaths%2F~1processes%2Fpost) request. The request payload would take the following shape:
{
"processDescription": {
"process": {
"id": "my-process-literal-package"
}
},
"executionUnit": [
{
"unit": {
"cwlVersion": "v1.0",
"class": "CommandLineTool",
"inputs": ["<...>"],
"outputs": ["<...>"],
"<...>": "<...>"
}
}
]
}
[Package as External Execution Unit Reference](#id111)[](#package-as-external-execution-unit-reference)
In this situation, the [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL) is provided indirectly using an external file reference which is expected to have
contents describing the [Application Package](appendix.html#term-Application-Package) (as presented in the [Package as Literal Execution Unit Block](#app-pkg-exec-unit-literal) case).
Because an external file is employed instead of embedding the package within the [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON) HTTP request contents,
it is possible to employ both [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON) and [YAML](appendix.html#term-YAML) definitions.
An example is presented below:
{
"processDescription": {
"process": {
"id": "my-process-reference-package"
}
},
"executionUnit": [
{
"href": "https://remote-file-server.com/my-package.cwl"
}
]
}
Where the referenced file hosted at "https://remote-file-server.com/my-package.cwl" could contain:
cwlVersion: "v1.0"
class: CommandLineTool
inputs:
- "<...>"
outputs:
- "<...>"
"<...>": "<...>"
[Package as Multiple CWL Documents](#id112)[](#package-as-multiple-cwl-documents)
When deploying a [Workflow](appendix.html#term-Workflow) with multiple dependent [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL) tools, Weaver supports
the multipart/related content format as defined in [OGC API - Processes - Part 2: Deploy, Replace, Undeploy](https://github.com/opengeospatial/ogcapi-processes/tree/master/extensions/deploy_replace_undeploy).
This allows packaging multiple [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL) documents in a single HTTP request using standard MIME multipart encoding.
The key advantage of this approach is that users can develop and test their [Workflow](appendix.html#term-Workflow) locally using
separate [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL) files, then deploy them as-is to Weaver without manual modifications. In contrast,
[CWL Packed Documents](https://www.commonwl.org/v1.2/Workflow.html#Packed_documents) (using $graph) or nested tool definitions require manual consolidation and
restructuring of multiple files into a single document before deployment.
Note
Users do not need to manually construct the multipart/related request format. The [CLI](cli.html#cli) and
[Python client](cli.html#client-commands) automatically handle multipart encoding and boundary generation
when multiple [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL) files are provided, making the deployment process seamless.
Weaver also supports [CWL Packed Documents](https://www.commonwl.org/v1.2/Workflow.html#Packed_documents) via $graph arrays if needed. Both the multipart approach
and $graph approach ultimately resolve to equivalent internal representations, so users can choose
whichever method best fits their workflow development process.
See also
For automated multi-CWL deployment using the CLI, refer to [Deploy Example](cli.html#cli-example-deploy).
Note
For HTTP API requests, use multipart/related content format to package multiple [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL) documents
in a single request body. See [CWL Multipart Content](package.html#app-pkg-multipart) for detailed examples and structure.
[ESGF-CWT](#id113)[](#esgf-cwt)
For [ESGF-CWT](appendix.html#term-ESGF-CWT) processes, the ESGF-CWTRequirement must be used in the [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL) hints section.
Using hints allows the [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL) content to be parsed even if the schema reference is missing.
This can be useful for deploying the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) on other instances not implemented with Weaver.
Note however that executing the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) in such case will most potentially fail unless the other implementation
handles it with custom logic.
To define the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) with explicit [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL) schema validation, the requirements section must be used
instead. To resolve the schema, the value weaver:ESGF-CWTRequirement should be used instead.
For an example [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL) using this definition, see [Remote Applications](package.html#app-pkg-esgf-cwt) section.
This kind of [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) allows for remote [Execution](#proc-op-execute) and
[Monitoring](#proc-op-monitor) of a [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) dispatched to an instance that
implements [ESGF Compute API](https://github.com/ESGF/esgf-compute-api) part of the [Earth System Grid Federation](https://esgf.github.io/).
Using Weaver, this [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) automatically obtains an [OGC API - Processes (WPS-REST, WPS-T, WPS-3)](#proc-ogc-api) representation.
[Workflow](#id114)[](#workflow)
Processes categorized as [Workflow](appendix.html#term-Workflow) are very similar to [OGC API - Processes (WPS-REST, WPS-T, WPS-3)](#proc-wps-rest) processes. From the API standpoint,
they actually look exactly the same as an atomic process when calling [DescribeProcess](#proc-op-describe)
or [Execute](#proc-op-execute) requests.
The difference lies within the referenced [Application Package](package.html#id1) which uses a [CWL Workflow](package.html#app-pkg-workflow) instead of
typical [CWL CommandLineTool](package.html#app-pkg-cmd), and therefore, modifies how the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) is internally executed.
For [Workflow](appendix.html#term-Workflow) processes to be deploy-able and executable, it is mandatory that Weaver is configured as
[EMS](appendix.html#term-EMS) or [HYBRID](appendix.html#term-HYBRID) (see: [Configuration Settings](configuration.html#configuration-settings)). This requirement is due to the nature
of [Workflow](appendix.html#term-Workflow) that chain processes that need to be dispatched to known remote [ADES](appendix.html#term-ADES) servers
(see: [Configuration of Data Sources](configuration.html#conf-data-sources) and [Workflow Step Operations](#proc-workflow-ops)) according to defined [Data Source](appendix.html#term-Data-Source) configuration.
Given that a [Workflow](appendix.html#term-Workflow) process was successfully deployed and that all process steps can be resolved, calling
its [Execute](#proc-op-execute) request will tell Weaver to parse the chain of operations and send step process
execution requests to relevant [ADES](appendix.html#term-ADES) picked according to [Data Source](appendix.html#term-Data-Source). Each step’s job will then gradually
be monitored from the relevant [ADES](appendix.html#term-ADES) until completion.
Upon successful intermediate result, the [EMS](appendix.html#term-EMS) (or [HYBRID](appendix.html#term-HYBRID) acting as such) will stage the data references
locally to chain them to the following step. When the complete chain succeeds, the final results of the last step will
be provided as [Workflow](appendix.html#term-Workflow) output in the same manner as for atomic processes. In case of failure, the error will
be indicated in the logs with the appropriate step and message where the error occurred.
Note
Although chaining sub-workflow(s) within a bigger scoped [Workflow](appendix.html#term-Workflow) is technically possible, this have not yet
been fully explored (tested) in Weaver. There is a chance that [Data Source](#data-source) resolution fails to identify where
to dispatch the step in this situation. If this impacts you, please vote and indicate your concern on issue
[#171](https://github.com/crim-ca/weaver/issues/171).
See also
[Workflow Step Operations](#proc-workflow-ops) provides more details on each of the internal operations accomplished by
individual step [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) chained in a [Workflow](appendix.html#term-Workflow).
[Remote Provider](#id115)[](#remote-provider)
A remote [Provider](appendix.html#term-Provider) corresponds to a service hosted remotely that provides similar or compatible
([WPS](appendix.html#term-WPS)-like) interfaces supported by Weaver. For example, a remote [WPS](appendix.html#term-WPS)-1 [XML](appendix.html#term-XML) endpoint
can be referenced as a [Provider](appendix.html#term-Provider). When an API [Providers](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Providers)-scoped request is executed, for example to list its
process capabilities (see [GetCapabilities](#proc-op-getcap)), Weaver will send the corresponding request using
the reference URL from the registered [Provider](appendix.html#term-Provider) to access the remote server and reply with the parsed response,
as if its processes were registered locally.
Since remote providers obviously require access to the remote service, Weaver will only be able to provide results if the service is accessible with respect to standard implementation features and supported specifications.
The main advantage of using Weaver’s endpoint rather than directly accessing the referenced remote [Provider](appendix.html#term-Provider)
processes is to palliate the limited functionalities offered by the service. For instance, [WPS](appendix.html#term-WPS)-1 do not always
offer [Monitoring a Job Execution (GetStatus)](#proc-op-status) feature, and there is no extensive [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) monitoring capabilities. Since Weaver
effectively wraps the referenced [Provider](appendix.html#term-Provider) with its own endpoints, these features indirectly become employable
through an extended [OGC API - Processes](appendix.html#term-OGC-API-Processes) interface. Similarly, although many [WPS](appendix.html#term-WPS)-1 offer [XML](appendix.html#term-XML)-only
responses, the parsing operation accomplished by Weaver makes theses services available as [WPS-REST](appendix.html#term-WPS-REST)
[JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON) endpoints with automatic conversion. On top of that, registering a remote [Provider](appendix.html#term-Provider) into Weaver
allows the user to use it as a central hub to keep references to all his remotely accessible services and dispatch
[Job](appendix.html#term-Job) executions from a common location.
A remote provider differs from previously presented [WPS-1/2](#proc-wps-12) processes such that the underlying processes
of the service are not registered locally. For example, if a remote service has two WPS processes, only top-level
service URL will be registered locally (in Weaver’s database) and the application will have no explicit knowledge
of these remote processes until requested. When calling [Process](appendix.html#term-Process)-specific requests
(e.g.: [DescribeProcess](#proc-op-describe) or [Execute](#proc-op-execute)), Weaver will re-send the
corresponding request (with appropriate interface conversion) directly to the remote [Provider](appendix.html#term-Provider) each time and
return the result accordingly. On the other hand, a [WPS-1/2](#proc-wps-12) reference would be parsed and saved locally with
the response at the time of deployment. This means that a deployed [WPS-1/2](#proc-wps-12) reference would act as
a snapshot of the reference [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) (which could become out-of-sync), while [Remote Provider](#proc-remote-provider) will
dynamically update according to the re-fetched response from the remote service each time, always keeping the obtained
description in sync with the remote [Provider](appendix.html#term-Provider). If our example remote service was extended to have a third
[WPS](appendix.html#term-WPS) process, it would immediately and transparently be reflected in [GetCapabilities](#proc-op-getcap)
and [DescribeProcess](#proc-op-describe) retrieved by Weaver on [Providers](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Providers)-scoped requests without any change
to the registered [Provider](appendix.html#term-Provider) definition. This would not be the case for the [WPS-1/2](#proc-wps-12) reference that
would need a manual update (i.e.: deploy the third [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) to register it in Weaver).
An example body of the [register provider](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Providers%2Fpaths%2F~1providers%2Fpost) request could be as follows:
{
"id": "my-service",
"url": "https://example.com/wps",
"public": true
}
Then, processes of this registered [Remote Provider](#proc-remote-provider) will be accessible. For example, if the referenced
service by the above URL add a WPS process identified by my-process, its JSON description would be obtained with
following request ([DescribeProviderProcess](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Provider-Processes%2Fpaths%2F~1providers~1%7Bprovider_id%7D~1processes~1%7Bprocess_id%7D%2Fget)):
GET {WEAVER_URL}/providers/my-service/processes/my-process
Note
Process my-process in the example is not registered locally. From the point of view of Weaver’s processes
(i.e.: route /processes/{id}), it does NOT exist. You must absolutely use the provider-prefixed route
/providers/{id}/processes/{id} to explicitly fetch and resolve this remote process definition.
Warning
API requests scoped under [Providers](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Providers) are Weaver-specific implementation. These are not part of [OGC API - Processes](https://github.com/opengeospatial/ogcapi-processes)
specification.
[Managing Processes included in Weaver ADES/EMS](#id116)[](#managing-processes-included-in-weaver-ades-ems)
Following steps represent the typical steps applied to deploy a process, execute it and retrieve the results.
[Register a New Process (Deploy)](#id117)[](#register-a-new-process-deploy)
Deployment of a new process is accomplished through the [ POST {WEAVER_URL}/processes (Deploy)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Processes%2Fpaths%2F~1processes%2Fpost) request.
See also
[OGC API - Processes - Part 2: Deploy, Replace, Undeploy](https://github.com/opengeospatial/ogcapi-processes/tree/master/extensions/deploy_replace_undeploy) specification.
The request body requires mainly two components:
- processDescription:Defines the- [Process](appendix.html#term-Process)identifier, metadata, inputs, outputs, and some execution specifications. This mostly corresponds to additional information that is provided by traditional- [WPS](appendix.html#term-WPS)or- [OGC API - Processes](appendix.html#term-OGC-API-Processes)definitions. A notable situation when this is required is when the following- executionUnitcannot directly resolve certain definitions specific to- [OGC API - Processes](appendix.html#term-OGC-API-Processes), such as a- [Media-Type](appendix.html#term-Media-Type)or- [File Format](package.html#cwl-file-format)not explicitly handled by- [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL).
- executionUnit:Defines the core details of the- [Application Package](docs/source/package.rst). This corresponds to the explicit- [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL)definition or other- [Type of Processes](#proc-types)references that indicates how to execute the underlying application.
Note
If the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) can be directly represented and converted from the [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL), it
can be directly deployed (i.e.: provided as is rather than embedding it in executionUnit) when combined with
the appropriate application/cwl+json or application/cwl+yaml [Media-Type](appendix.html#term-Media-Type) in Content-Type header.
Note
For deploying multiple related [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL) packages (e.g., a [Workflow](appendix.html#term-Workflow) with dependent tools),
the multipart/related [Media-Type](appendix.html#term-Media-Type) can be used in the Content-Type header to package
all [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL) documents in a single request. Each part should specify its own content type
(application/cwl+json or application/cwl+yaml) and unique Content-ID.
See [Package as Multiple CWL Documents](#proc-ogc-api-multi-cwl) and [CWL Multipart Content](package.html#app-pkg-multipart) for detailed multipart structure and examples.
Note
Multiple [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL) packages can also be deployed using an array of executionUnit entries, where each
entry contains either an inline unit object or an href reference to an external [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL) document.
This approach resolves the multi-[CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL) references in an equivalent fashion to the multipart/related
content case described above, but allows deployment through standard [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON) request bodies without
requiring multipart encoding. Only [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL)-like [Media-Types](appendix.html#term-Media-Types) are accepted to avoid ambiguities
with other deployment formats (e.g.: application/json or application/ogcapppkg+json).
See also
Section [Correspondence between CWL and WPS fields](package.html#cwl-wps-mapping) provides further details about notable considerations that
could require additional fields in processDescription for an adequate [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) definition.
Upon deploy request, Weaver will either respond with a successful result, or with the appropriate error message, whether caused by conflicting ID, invalid definitions or other parsing issues. A successful process deployment will result in this process to become available for following steps.
Warning
When a process is deployed, it is not necessarily available immediately. This is because process visibility also
needs to be updated. The process must be made public to allow its discovery. Alternatively, the visibility can
be directly provided within the body of the deploy request to skip this extra step.
For specifying or updating visibility, please refer to corresponding [ POST {WEAVER_URL}/processes (Deploy)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Processes%2Fpaths%2F~1processes%2Fpost) and
[requests.](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Processes%2Fpaths%2F~1processes~1%7Bprocess_id%7D~1visibility%2Fput)
PUT {WEAVER_URL}/processes/{processID}/visibility (Visibility)After deployment and visibility preconditions have been met, the corresponding process should become available
through [DescribeProcess](#proc-op-describe) requests and other routes that depend on an existing process.
Note that when a process is deployed using the [OGC API - Processes (WPS-REST, WPS-T, WPS-3)](#proc-wps-rest) interface, it also becomes available through the
[WPS-1/2](#proc-wps-12) interface with the same identifier and definition. Because of compatibility limitations, some
parameters in the [WPS-1/2](#proc-wps-12) side might not be perfectly mapped to the equivalent or adjusted
[OGC API - Processes (WPS-REST, WPS-T, WPS-3)](#proc-wps-rest) interface, although this concerns mostly only new features such as [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) status monitoring.
For most traditional use cases, properties are mapped between the two interfaces, but it is recommended to use the
[OGC API - Processes (WPS-REST, WPS-T, WPS-3)](#proc-wps-rest) one because of the added features.
See also
Please refer to [application-package](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/package.html#application-package) chapter for any additional parameters that can be
provided for specific types of [Application Package](appendix.html#term-Application-Package) and [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) definitions.
[Access Registered Processes (GetCapabilities, DescribeProcess)](#id118)[](#access-registered-processes-getcapabilities-describeprocess)
Available processes can all be listed using [ GET {WEAVER_URL}/processes (GetCapabilities)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Processes%2Fpaths%2F~1processes%2Fget) request. This request will return all locally registered
process summaries. Other return formats and filters are also available according to provided request query parameters.
Note that processes not marked with public visibility will not be listed in this result.
For more specific process details, the [ GET {WEAVER_URL}/processes/{processID} (DescribeProcess)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Processes%2Fpaths%2F~1processes~1%7Bprocess_id%7D~1package%2Fget) request should be used. This will return all information
that define the process references and expected inputs/outputs.
Note
For remote processes (see: [Remote Provider](#remote-provider)), [Provider requests](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Providers) are also available for more fine-grained
search of underlying processes. These processes are not necessarily listed as local processes, and will therefore
sometime not yield any result if using the typical DescribeProcess request on wps_endpoint.
All routes listed under [Process requests](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Processes) should normally be applicable for remote processes by prefixing
them with /providers/{id}.
Changed in version 4.20.
With the addition of [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) revisions (see [Update Operation](#proc-op-update) below), a registered
[Process](appendix.html#term-Process) specified only by {processID} will retrieve the latest revision of that [Process](appendix.html#term-Process).
A specific older revision can be obtained by adding the tagged version in the path ({processID}:{version}) or
adding the request query parameter version.
Using revisions provided through PUT and PATCH requests, it is also possible to list specific or all existing
revisions of a given or multiple processes simultaneously using the revisions and version query parameters with
the [ GET {WEAVER_URL}/processes (GetCapabilities)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Processes%2Fpaths%2F~1processes%2Fget) request.
[Modify an Existing Process (Update, Replace, Undeploy)](#id119)[](#modify-an-existing-process-update-replace-undeploy)
Added in version 4.20.
Since Weaver supports [OGC API - Processes - Part 2: Deploy, Replace, Undeploy](https://github.com/opengeospatial/ogcapi-processes/tree/master/extensions/deploy_replace_undeploy), it is able to remove a previously registered [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) using
the [Deployment](#proc-op-deploy) request. The undeploy operation consist of a DELETE request targeting the
specific {WEAVER_URL}/processes/{processID} to be removed.
Note
The [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) must be accessible by the user considering any visibility configuration to perform this step.
See [Register a New Process (Deploy)](#proc-op-deploy) section for details.
Starting from version [4.20](https://github.com/crim-ca/weaver/tree/4.20.0), a [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) can be replaced or
updated using respectively the PUT and PATCH requests onto the specific {WEAVER_URL}/processes/{processID}
location of the reference to modify.
Note
The [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) partial update operation (using PATCH) is specific to Weaver only.
[OGC API - Processes - Part 2: Deploy, Replace, Undeploy](https://github.com/opengeospatial/ogcapi-processes/tree/master/extensions/deploy_replace_undeploy) only mandates the definition of PUT request for full override of a [Process](appendix.html#term-Process).
When a [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) is modified using the PATCH operation, only the new definitions need to be provided, and
unspecified items are transferred over from the referenced [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) (i.e.: the previous revision). Using either
the PUT or PATCH requests, previous revisions can be referenced using two formats:
- {processID}:{version}as request path parameters (instead of usual- {processID}only)
- {processID}in the request path combined with- ?version={version}query parameter
Weaver employs MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH semantic versioning to maintain revisions of updated or replaced [Process](appendix.html#term-Process)
definitions. The next revision number to employ for update or replacement can either be provided explicitly in the
request body using a version, or be omitted. When omitted, the next revision will be guessed automatically based
on the previous available revision according to the level of changes required. In either cases, the resolved version
will have to be available and respect the expected update level to be accepted as a new valid [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) revision.
The applicable revision level depends on the contents being modified using submitted request body fields according
to the following table. When a combination of the below items occur, the higher update level is required.
| HTTP Method | Level | Change | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|
|
|
| Modifications to metadata
not impacting the
| |
|
|
| Modification that impacts
how the | |
|
|
| Modification that impacts
what the |
|
Note
For all applicable fields of updating a [Process](appendix.html#term-Process), refer to the schema of [ PATCH {WEAVER_URL}/processes/{processID} (Update)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Processes/paths/~1processes~1{process_id}/patch).
For replacing a
[Process](appendix.html#term-Process), refer instead to the schema of
[. The replacement request contents are extremely similar to the](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Processes/paths/~1processes~1{process_id}/put)
PUT {WEAVER_URL}/processes/{processID} (Replace)[Deploy](#proc-op-deploy)schema since the full
[Process](appendix.html#term-Process)definition must be provided.
For example, if the test-process:1.2.3 was previously deployed, and is the active latest revision of that
[Process](appendix.html#term-Process), submitting the below request body will produce a PATCH revision as test-process:1.2.4.
PATCH /processes/test-process:1.2.3 HTTP/1.1
Host: weaver.example.com
Content-Type: application/json
{
"description": "new description",
"inputs": {
"input": {
"description": "modified input description"
},
"outputs": {
"output": {
"title": "modified title"
}
}
}
}
Here, only metadata is adjusted and there is no risk to impact produced results or execution methods of the
[Process](appendix.html#term-Process). An external user would probably not even notice the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) changed, which is why PATCH
is reasonable in this case. Notice that the version is not explicitly provided in the body. It is guessed
automatically from the modified contents. Also, the example displays how [Process](appendix.html#term-Process)-level and
inputs/outputs-level metadata can be updated.
Similarly, the following request would produce a MINOR revision of test-process. Since both PATCH and
MINOR level contents are defined for update, the higher MINOR revision is required. In this case MINOR is
required because jobControlOptions (forced to [asynchronous](#proc-exec-mode) execution for following versions) would break any
future request made by users that would expect the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) to run (or support) [synchronous](#proc-exec-mode) execution.
Notice that this time, the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) reference does not indicate the revision in the path (no :1.2.4 part).
This automatically resolves to the updated revision test-process:1.2.4 that became the new latest revision following
our previous PATCH request.
PATCH /processes/test-process HTTP/1.1
Host: weaver.example.com
Content-Type: application/json
{
"description": "process async only",
"jobControlOptions": ["async-execute"],
"version": "1.4.0"
}
In this case, the desired version (1.4.0) is also specified explicitly in the body. Since the updated number
(MINOR = 4) matches the expected update level from the above table and respects an higher level than the reference
1.2.4 [Process](appendix.html#term-Process), this revision value will be accepted (instead of auto-resolved 1.3.0 otherwise). Note
that if 2.4.0 was specified instead, the version would be refused, as Weaver does not consider this modification
to be worth a MAJOR revision, and tries to keep version levels consistent. Skipping numbers (i.e.: 1.3.0 in this
case), is permitted as long as there are no other versions above of the same level (i.e.: 1.4.0 would be refused if
1.5.0 existed). This allows some level of flexibility with revisions in case users want to use specific numbering
values that have more meaning to them. It is recommended to let Weaver auto-update version values between updates if
this level of fined-grained control is not required.
Note
To avoid conflicting definitions, a [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) cannot be [Deployed](#proc-op-deploy) directly using a
{processID}:{version} reference. Deployments are expected as the first revision and should only include the
{processID} portion as their identifier.
If the user desires a specific version to deploy, the PUT request should be used with the appropriate version
within the request body. However, it is up to the user to provide the full definition of that updated [Process](appendix.html#term-Process),
since PUT request will “replace” the updated definition from scratch, taking exactly the contents provided in
the request, rather than transfer over missing parameters from the old [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) (i.e: as PATCH request does).
Even when a [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) is “replaced” using PUT, the older revision is not actually removed and undeployed
(DELETE request). Instead, the referenced processID is is replaced to its explicit {processID}:{version}
revision, and the new definition is swapped as the new processID reference. It is therefore still possible to refer
to the old revision using explicit references with the corresponding version, while the processID will appear
as “replaced” from the point of view of a client not aware of Weaver’s revision management.
Weaver keeps track of revisions by corresponding {processID} entries such that if the latest revision is
undeployed, the previous revision in semantic order will automatically become the latest once again. For complete
replacement, the user should instead perform a DELETE of all existing revisions (to avoid conflicts) followed by a
new [Deploy](#proc-op-deploy) request.
[Execution of a Process (Execute)](#id120)[](#execution-of-a-process-execute)
[Process](appendix.html#term-Process) execution (i.e.: submitting a [Job](appendix.html#term-Job)) is accomplished using the [ POST {WEAVER_URL}/processes/{processID}/execution (Execute)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Processes/paths/~1processes~1{process_id}~1execution/post) request.
Note
For backward compatibility, the [ POST {WEAVER_URL}/processes/{processID}/jobs (Execute)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Processes%2Fpaths%2F~1processes~1{process_id}~1jobs%2Fpost) request is also supported as alias to the above
[OGC API - Processes](appendix.html#term-OGC-API-Processes)compliant endpoint.
See also
Alternatively, the [ POST {WEAVER_URL}/jobs (Create)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Jobs/paths/~1jobs/post) request can also be used to submit a
[Job](appendix.html#term-Job)for later execution, as well as enabling other advanced
[Job Management](#proc-job-management)capabilities. See
[Submitting a Job Creation](#proc-op-job-create)for more details.
This section will first describe the basics of this request format ([Execution Body](#proc-exec-body)), and after go into
further details for specific use cases and parametrization of various input/output combinations
([Execution Mode](#proc-exec-mode), [Execution Results](#proc-exec-results), etc.).
Below are some examples of [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON) body that can be sent to the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) execution endpoint to
better illustrate where each of the mentioned parameters in following sections are expected.
| {
"mode": "async",
"response": "document",
"inputs": [
{
"id": "input-file",
"href": "<file-reference>"
},
{

"data": 1,
}
],

Note
For backward compatibility, the execution payload inputs and outputs can be provided either as mapping
(keys are the IDs, values are the content), or as listing (each item has content and "id" field)
interchangeably. When working with [OGC API - Processes](appendix.html#term-OGC-API-Processes) compliant services, the mapping representation
should be preferred as it is the official schema, is more compact, and it allows inline specification of literal
data (values provided without the nested value field). The listing representation is the older format employed
during previous [OGC](appendix.html#term-OGC) testbed developments.
See also
Many additional parameters can be used to request further functionalities. The above fields only present the

Changed in version 4.20.
With the addition of [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) revisions (see [Update Operation](#proc-op-update) section), a registered
[Process](appendix.html#term-Process) specified only by {processID} will execute the latest revision of that [Process](appendix.html#term-Process). An older
revision can be executed by adding the tagged version in the path ({processID}:{version}) or adding the request
query parameter version.
[Execution Body](#id121)[](#execution-body)
The inputs definition is the most important section of the request body. It is also the only one that is completely
required when submitting the execution request, even for a no-input process (an empty mapping is needed in such case).
It defines which parameters
to forward to the referenced [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) to be executed. All id elements in this [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) request
body must correspond to valid inputs from the definition returned by [DescribeProcess](#proc-op-describe)
response. Obviously, all formatting requirements (i.e.: proper file [Media-Types](appendix.html#term-Media-Types)),
data types (e.g.: int, string, etc.) and validations rules (e.g.: minOccurs, AllowedValues, etc.)
must also be fulfilled. When providing files as input,
multiple protocols are supported. See later section [File Reference Types](#file-reference-types) for details.
The outputs section defines, for each id available from the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) definition, how to
report the produced outputs from a successful [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) execution. The method under which each output will
be returned depends on the negotiated [Execution Mode](#proc-exec-mode) and [Execution Results](#proc-exec-results).
When an output corresponds to a [File Reference](#file-ref-types) produced by the [Application Package](appendix.html#term-Application-Package),
and stored locally, the result will typically (unless requested otherwise), be exposed externally using the returned
reference [URL](appendix.html#term-URL).
For outputs that correspond to literal data, such as plain strings or numbers, Weaver will typically prefer
returning the value directly. However, alternate link representations can also be obtained if specified in the
execution request, using transmissionMode overrides for the desired outputs.
Execution Body Outputs Filtering[](#execution-body-outputs-filtering)
When the outputs section is omitted, it simply means that the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) to be executed
should return all outputs it offers in the created [Job Results](#proc-op-result).
If the outputs section is specified, but that one of the requested outputs [[1]](#outn) defined in
the [Process Description](#proc-op-describe) is not specified, this indicates that the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) should
omit this output from the produced results. When requested outputs are specified without any transmissionMode,
the reference representation is used automatically for [File Reference](#file-ref-types) as it makes all
outputs more easily accessible with distinct [URL](appendix.html#term-URL) afterwards, and value is used for literal data to
obtain them directly (inline in the response). Opposite value/reference representations can be requested
explicitly, for each respective output, using the transmissionMode as presented below.
Warning
When using outputs in the request body, one necessarily introduces filtering indications of results to
be returned. If all outputs are desired, some of which override transmissionMode and others letting
their representation auto-resolve, explicit {} mapping must be indicated to avoid filtering them out.
{
"inputs": {"<...>": "<...>"},
"outputs": {
"output-default": {},
"output-by-value": {"transmissionMode": "value"},
"output-by-ref": {"transmissionMode": "reference"}
}
}
When transmissionMode is specified for a given output, its result representation will override any other
parameter that would otherwise affect its automatic or “informed” resolution of the output representation.
These parameters are further detailed in the following [Execution Mode](#proc-exec-mode) and [Execution Results](#proc-exec-results) sections.
[Execution Mode](#id122)[](#execution-mode)
In order to select how to execute a [Process](appendix.html#term-Process), either [synchronously](#proc-exec-mode) or [asynchronously](#proc-exec-mode), the Prefer header
should be specified. If omitted, Weaver defaults to [asynchronous](#proc-exec-mode) execution. To execute [asynchronously](#proc-exec-mode)
explicitly, Prefer: respond-async should be used. Otherwise, the [synchronous](#proc-exec-mode) execution can be requested
with Prefer: wait=X where X is the duration in seconds to wait for a response. If no worker becomes available
within that time, or if this value is greater than
the weaver.execute_sync_max_wait setting (see [detail](configuration.html#weaver-execute-sync-max-wait)), the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) will
resume [asynchronously](#proc-exec-mode) and the response will be returned. Furthermore, [synchronous](#proc-exec-mode) and [asynchronous](#proc-exec-mode) execution of
a [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) can only be requested for corresponding jobControlOptions it reports as supported in
its [Process Description](#proc-op-describe). It is important to provide the jobControlOptions parameter with
applicable modes when [Deploying a Process](#proc-op-deploy) to allow it to run as desired. By default, Weaver
will assume that deployed processes are only [asynchronous](#proc-exec-mode) to handle longer operations.
Changed in version 4.15: By default, every [Builtin](#proc-builtin) [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) can accept both modes.
All previously deployed processes will only allow [asynchronous](#proc-exec-mode) execution, as only this one was supported.
This should be reported in their jobControlOptions.
Warning
It is important to remember that the Prefer header is indeed a preference. If Weaver deems it cannot
allocate a worker to execute the task [synchronously](#proc-exec-mode) within a reasonable delay, it can enforce the [asynchronous](#proc-exec-mode)
execution. The [asynchronous](#proc-exec-mode) mode is also prioritized for running longer [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) submitted over the task
queue, as this allows Weaver to offer better availability for all requests submitted by its users.
The [synchronous](#proc-exec-mode) mode should be reserved only for very quick and relatively low computation intensive operations.

The mode field displayed in the [Example Job Execution Request Body](#table-exec-body) is another method to tell whether to run the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process)
in a blocking (sync) or non-blocking (async) manner. Note that support is limited for mode sync as this use
case is often more cumbersome than async execution. Effectively, sync mode requires to have a task worker
executor available to run the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) (otherwise it fails immediately due to lack of processing resource), and
the requester must wait for the whole execution to complete to obtain the result.
Given that [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) could take a very long time to complete, it is not practical to execute them in this
manner and potentially have to wait hours to retrieve outputs.
Instead, the preferred and default approach is to request an async [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) execution. When doing so, Weaver
will add this to a task queue for processing, and will immediately return a [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) identifier and Location
where the user can probe for its status, using [Monitoring](#proc-op-monitor) request. As soon as any task worker
becomes available, it will pick any leftover queued [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) to execute it.
Note
The mode field is an older methodology that precedes the latest [OGC API - Processes](appendix.html#term-OGC-API-Processes) method using
the Prefer header. It is recommended to employ the Prefer header that ensures higher interoperability
with other services using the same standard. The mode field is deprecated and preserved only for backward
compatibility purpose.
When requesting a [synchronous](#proc-exec-mode) execution, and provided a worker was available to pick and complete the task before
the maximum wait time was reached, the final status will be directly returned. Therefore, the contents obtained this
way will be identical to any following [Job Status](#proc-op-status) request. If no worker is available, or if
the worker that picked the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) cannot complete it in time (either because it takes too long to execute or had
to wait on resources for too long), the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) execution will automatically switch to [asynchronous](#proc-exec-mode) mode.
The distinction between an [asynchronous](#proc-exec-mode) or [synchronous](#proc-exec-mode) response when executing a [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) can be
observed in multiple ways. The easiest is with the HTTP status code of the response, 200 being for
a [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) entirely completed synchronously, and 201 for a created [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) that should be
[monitored](#proc-op-monitor) asynchronously. Another method is to observe the "status" value.
Effectively, a [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) that is executed [asynchronously](#proc-exec-mode) will return status information contents, while
a [synchronous](#proc-exec-mode) [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) will return the results directly, along a Location header referring to the
equivalent contents returned by [GetStatus](#proc-op-status) as in the case of [asynchronous](#proc-exec-mode) [Job](appendix.html#term-Job).
It is also possible to extract the Preference-Applied response header which will clearly indicate if the
submitted Prefer header was respected (because it could be with available worker resources) or not.
In general, this means that if the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) submission request was not provided with Prefer: wait=X AND
replied with the same Preference-Applied value, it is safe to assume Weaver decided to queue the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job)
for [asynchronous](#proc-exec-mode) execution. That [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) could be executed immediately, or at a later time, according to
worker availability.
It is also possible that a failed [Job](appendix.html#term-Job), even when [synchronous](#proc-exec-mode), will respond with equivalent contents
to the status location instead of results. This is because it is impossible for Weaver to return
the result(s) as outputs would not be generated by the incomplete [Job](appendix.html#term-Job).
For any of the execution combinations, it is always possible to obtain [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) outputs,
along with logs, exceptions and other details using the [Obtaining Job Details and Metadata](#proc-op-result) endpoints.
[Execution Results](#id123)[](#execution-results)
When requesting a [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) execution, the structure under which the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) results are returned can
be adjusted using the Prefer header with the return parameter. More precisely, the Prefer: return=minimal
and Prefer: return=representation definitions can be used to control whether the resulting outputs would be
provided using link references, or directly using their raw data representation. This behavior is described by the
[OGC API - Processes](appendix.html#term-OGC-API-Processes) (v2.0) standard revision.
The previous [OGC API - Processes](appendix.html#term-OGC-API-Processes) (v1.0) standard revision instead made use of a combination of the response
and transmissionMode parameters in the execution request body, as previously shown in table [Example Job Execution Request Body](#table-exec-body).
In general, both approaches can be used interchangeably, but some combinations are not directly portable.
Whenever possible, it is recommended to employ the Prefer header that should provide higher interoperability
with latest service implementations using the same standard. However, given that transmissionMode and response
fields can allow more flexibility and strict control regarding how data is returned is specific edge cases, in contrast
to the Prefer header approach, both approaches remain available in Weaver.
See also
See the [opengeospatial/ogcapi-processes#412](https://github.com/opengeospatial/ogcapi-processes/issues/412)
discussions for more details about each approach, their considerations, and potential side-effects.

Important
Typically, clients will not use Prefer header and response/transmissionMode body parameters
simultaneously (although permitted), since they should be interchangeable in most situations.
The table indicates both [OGC API - Processes](appendix.html#term-OGC-API-Processes) v1.0/v2.0 variations to illustrate which combinations lead to the same result.
If a client happens to use both combination simultaneously, the body parameters will take precedence
over the Prefer header for conflicting cases. This is in order to respect the fact that body parameters
are “hard requirements”, whereas Prefer is a “soft requirement” (i.e.: a preference) that does not
necessarily need to be respected if the server cannot resolve the combination.
Important
It is important not to confuse expected Results above with Responses.
The actual HTTP Response returned from the execution endpoint will depend on the requested [Execution Mode](#proc-exec-mode).
A [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) successfully resolved with [synchronous](#proc-exec-mode) execution will return the Results shown in the table
directly with a HTTP 200 OK or HTTP 204 No Content status (as applicable), whereas an [asynchronous](#proc-exec-mode) execution
will always return a [Job Status](#proc-op-status) Response with HTTP 201 Created or HTTP 202 Accepted
status (accordingly if the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) started immediately or is still pending).
In the case of a successfully completed [asynchronous](#proc-exec-mode) execution, a
subsequent [Results Request](#proc-op-result) using the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) Location
is needed to obtain the Results presented in the above table.
Note that a [synchronous](#proc-exec-mode) execution can also
make use of the [Results Request](#proc-op-result) operation to obtain the outputs again at a later time, to
request alternate output representations, or retrieve additional [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) information such as logs and metadata.
Note
Combinations using <none> indicate that the parameter is omitted entirely from the request. When the value is provided but “does not matter” (i.e.: leading to the same outcome regardless), the <any> notation is used instead. The n/a notation indicates not applicable cases, due to a technical or logical impossibility.
Warning
When negotiating a single output as [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON), there is a potential ambiguity between
[Results](#proc-op-job-results) representation and a single file’s data, such as in the
case of a [GeoJSON](appendix.html#term-GeoJSON) structure, both of which are encoded in [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON).
Similar ambiguities could also occur for other [Media-Types](appendix.html#term-Media-Types), depending on supported formats,
such as representing [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) results in [XML](appendix.html#term-XML), or retrieving a file’s data encoded as GML [XML](appendix.html#term-XML).
To avoid ambiguity, it is recommended that the response: document or response: raw
is explicitly set for such cases to ensure the result matches the desired outcome.
In the event that the [Results Document](#job-results-document-minimal) representation is desired
as [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON) response for that single output result, [Content Negotiation by Profile](https://profilenegotiation.github.io/I-D-Profile-Negotiation/I-D-Profile-Negotiation) [[7]](#resprofile)
can be employed to remove the ambiguity. Other [Profile](appendix.html#term-Profile) definitions could be added to remove further
ambiguities with other [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON)-like structures, but these are not explicitly handled by Weaver at this time.
Details
In summary, the Prefer and response parameters define how to return the results produced by the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process).
The Prefer header is also used by [OGC API - Processes](appendix.html#term-OGC-API-Processes) v2.0 to control how the results are encoded, whereas v1.0 relies on a
separate transmissionMode parameter. By reducing the amount of parameters involved, v2.0 makes the request easier
to submit with a single header (also used to indicate the [Execution Mode](#proc-exec-mode)), but limits certain representation
combinations only possible with v1.0. These limited representations can be retrieved by involving more advanced
[Profile](appendix.html#term-Profile) and [Media-Type](appendix.html#term-Media-Type) [Content Negotiation](#proc-content-negotiation) techniques.
See also
Examples of typical contents for many of the combinations are provided under the [Job Results](#proc-op-job-results) section.
[Execution KVP-Encoded](#id124)[](#execution-kvp-encoded)
Added in version 6.10.0.
In addition to the [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON)-based [POST Process Execution](#proc-op-execute) requests, Weaver
supports [Key-Value Pair (KVP)](appendix.html#term-KVP) encoded [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) execution using HTTP GET requests.
This execution method is defined by the [OGC API - Processes - Part 1: Core KVP-Encoded Execute](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/18-062r3.html#rc_kvp-execute) definitions, allowing [Process](appendix.html#term-Process)
parameters to be specified directly in the [URL](appendix.html#term-URL) query string.
[KVP](appendix.html#term-KVP) execution provides an alternative approach to submitting [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) requests that can be more convenient
for simple executions, URL-based [Workflow](appendix.html#term-Workflow) sub-[Process](appendix.html#term-Process) invocations, or integration with systems that
prefer GET-based operations.
All [KVP](appendix.html#term-KVP) requests are converted internally to the equivalent [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON) execution format, ensuring consistent
behavior with POST-based executions.
See also
- [OGC API - Processes - Part 1: Core KVP-Encoded Execute](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/18-062r3.html#rc_kvp-execute)for the complete specification
- [Execution of a Process (Execute)](#proc-op-execute)for the equivalent POST-based execution method
[KVP](appendix.html#term-KVP) execution requests use the following endpoint:
GET /processes/{processID}/execution?<parameters> HTTP/1.1
Host: weaver.example.com
All execution <parameters> are provided as query string key-value pairs, using either direct values
and using extended bracket notation for additional qualifiers in the style of [OpenAPI](appendix.html#term-OpenAPI) deepObject queries.
?parameter[qualifier]=value
All parameter qualifiers are case-insensitive. The casing of the primary parameters depend of their context.
Certain parameters (notably response) are reserved for alignment with other [OGC API - Processes](https://github.com/opengeospatial/ogcapi-processes) requirements and
extensions, which therefore allow case-insensitive names. However, input and output identifiers directly mapped to the
[Process](appendix.html#term-Process) description parameters preserve their original case to ensure adequate resolution and avoid ambiguities.
Warning
This casing management is a non-standard [OGC API - Processes - Part 1: Core KVP-Encoded Execute](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/18-062r3.html#rc_kvp-execute) behavior enforced by Weaver
to ensure data integrity.
The values of the parameters are also case-sensitive as to not alter the intended meaning of the submitted values
for execution of the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process). However, adequate [URL](appendix.html#term-URL) encoding and escape mechanisms apply to ensure
that special characters are properly transmitted and parsed. Following should be considered for [URL](appendix.html#term-URL) encoding:
- Embedded - [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON)arrays (- [and- ]) conflicting with- [qualifier]notation
- Reserved characters in - [URL](appendix.html#term-URL)query strings (- &,- =) conflicting with- [KVP](appendix.html#term-KVP)separation
- Special - [URL](appendix.html#term-URL)characters such as- +,- %, and- #that require encoding to avoid misinterpretation

KVP Input Parameters[](#kvp-input-parameters)
Input values can be specified using multiple formats depending on their data type and requirements.
The following table shows [KVP](appendix.html#term-KVP) notation alongside their equivalent [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON) POST body representations.
Note
All inputs can be provided using [URL](appendix.html#term-URL)-encoded string as long as their decoded value results
into a valid [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON) structure. The values can be provided directly if there is no ambiguity between their
values and reserved [URL](appendix.html#term-URL) characters, including the explicit , comma separator representation below.
In other words, an array of numerics could be provided either
as arrayOfValues=[1,2,4,10,7] or arrayOfValues=%5B1%2C2%2C4%2C10%2C7%5D interchangeably.
For convenience, a comma-separated list of values (e.g.: arrayOfValues=1,2,4,10,7) is supported.
To avoid misinterpretation with the [URL](appendix.html#term-URL)-encoded [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON) structure, the commas must NOT be
[URL](appendix.html#term-URL)-encoded (i.e.: not %2C), but their nested values can employ escaped characters as needed.
For example, the value arrayOfSimpleValues=1,2%2C5,4,10%2C7 would be interpreted as an array of
values: [1, "2,5", 4, "10,7"]. Inputs will be converted to float or integer values when possible,
but will be kept as strings otherwise. If the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) requires float, explicit . could be
needed with the numeric values to ensure proper conversion.
Note
Bounding box coordinates are handled like the comma-separated array value above, but with additional
requirement of 2D or 3D coordinates (i.e.: 4 or 6 float values required). The order of these values depend entirely
on the relevant [crs] and defaults to the OGC:CRS84 (or OGC:CRS84h for 3D) in long [URI](appendix.html#term-URI) format,
with the expected WGS:84 ellipsoid using longitude-latitude coordinates lon1,lat1[,alt1],lon2,lat2[,alt2].
The [crs] qualifier should be provided to ensure correct interpretation of the coordinates [[8]](#kvpbboxnote).
Note
If necessary by the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) to interpret a certain input value correctly, a string may be
accompanied by contentMediaType, contentEncoding and contentSchema qualifiers to provide
additional context about the value’s content and structure.
Note
Binary data (typically a file) can be provided by-reference, by-value (i.e.: {inputID}={binary-data}),
or using Qualified Value (using the [value] and other optional format encoding qualifiers).

KVP Output Parameters[](#kvp-output-parameters)
Specific outputs can be requested and their format controlled using bracket notation qualifiers.
Warning
The [include] qualifier is required to request an output. This is to ensure that it can be distinguished
from [KVP Input Parameters](#proc-exec-kvp-inputs) identifiers. Additional format qualifiers are optional and can be combined as
needed.
Similarly to [Execution Body Outputs Filtering](#proc-exec-body-outputs-filtering) in the [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON) POST body request case, including
any {outputID}[include]=true parameter triggers the filtering behaviour, which means any other outputs will be
omitted from the response. If other outputs are desired, they must be explicitly included with their
own [include] parameter. If no outputs are indicated, the response will omit all outputs available from
the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) (i.e.: empty response [[2]](#resnocontent)). If desired, the request can be explicit by
indicating {outputID}[include]=false for outputs that should be omitted, but this is not required since
it is the default behaviour.
The following table shows [KVP](appendix.html#term-KVP) notation alongside their equivalent [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON) POST body representations.
| KVP Query Parameters | Equivalent JSON Body |
|---|---|
| Basic Output Selection | |
| ?output1[include]=true
&output2[include]=false
| {
"outputs": {
"output1": {}
}
}
|
| Output with Format Control | |
| ?result[include]=true
&result[mediaType]=application/json
&result[encoding]=gzip
| {
"outputs": {
"result": {
"format": {
"mediaType": "application/json",
"encoding": "gzip"
}
}
}
}
|
| Output with Schema | |
| ?data[include]=true
&data[schema]=http://example.com/schema.json
| {
"outputs": {
"data": {
"format": {
"schema": "http://example.com/schema.json"
}
}
}
}
|
| Output with Profile | |
| ?result[include]=true
&result[mediaType]=application/geo%2Bjson
&result[profile]=geojson-feature
| {

"mediaType": "application/geo+json",
"profile": "geojson-feature"
}

KVP Response Parameters[](#kvp-response-parameters)
Response format and execution preferences can be controlled using response bracket notation parameters.
These map directly to HTTP headers for consistent behavior across GET and POST execution methods.
| KVP Query Parameters | Equivalent HTTP Header |
|---|---|
| Response Format (short form) | |
| ?response[f]=application/json
| Accept: application/json
|
| Response Format (explicit alias) | |
| ?response[format]=application/json
| Accept: application/json
|
| Response Profile (for | |
| ?response[profile]=[ogc-rel:results]
| Accept-Profile: [ogc-rel:results]
|
| Execution Preference (async) | |
| ?response[prefer]=respond-async
| Prefer: respond-async
|
| Execution Preference (sync with timeout) | |
| ?response[prefer]=wait=30
| Prefer: wait=30
|
[1](#id42),
[2](#id46))
The behavior of [Profile](appendix.html#term-Profile) parameters vary depending on [Execution Mode](#proc-exec-mode).
Warning
The profile and response[profile] parameters have different implications depending on the
[Execution Mode](#proc-exec-mode). Other precaution must also be taken to avoid confusion
between these parameters and the other [profile] qualifiers used for inputs and outputs.
- Synchronous Execution (Prefer: wait):
- Both - profileand- response[profile]are equivalent and apply to the same immediate response containing the- [Execution Results](#proc-exec-results). They can be used interchangeably because the response return directly from the execution request.
- Asynchronous Execution (Prefer: respond-async):
- profileapplies to the- [Job Status](#proc-op-status)response (the immediate HTTP 201 Created response)
- response[profile]applies to the final- [Execution Results](#proc-exec-results)(retrieved by subsequent- [Job Result](#proc-op-result)request) This can be relevant the profile of the results as a whole is relevant (e.g.:- response[profile]=stac), such as when combined with the- response=collectionparameter.
- Input/Output Profile Qualifiers ({inputID}[profile],{outputID}[profile]):
- These format qualifiers are independent of - [Execution Mode](#proc-exec-mode)and always specify the content- [Profile](appendix.html#term-Profile)for those specific inputs or outputs, regardless of whether execution is- [synchronous](#proc-exec-mode)or- [asynchronous](#proc-exec-mode).
Example for Asynchronous Execution:
?...
&input[href]=http://example.com/data.json
&input[type]=application/geo%2Bjson
&input[profile]=http://www.opengis.net/def/format/ogcapi-processes/0/geojson-geometry
&output[include]=true
&output[profile]=http://www.opengis.net/def/format/ogcapi-processes/0/geojson-feature-collection
&response=collection
&response[profile]=http://www.opengis.net/def/format/ogcapi-processes/0/stac
&response[prefer]=respond-async
&profile=ogc
&f=json
In this example, the immediate [Job Status](#proc-op-status) is obtained [asynchronously](#proc-exec-mode), and explicitly
requests its [OGC](appendix.html#term-OGC) representation (rather than [openEO](appendix.html#term-openEO) for example), and requests it to be returned
in [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON) (rather than [YAML](appendix.html#term-YAML) for example).
It requests that the [Job Result](#proc-op-result) from that execution to be represented as a [STAC](appendix.html#term-STAC)
collection (e.g.: to include relevant metadata and assets specific to it), although the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) itself
is expected to produce a [GeoJSON](appendix.html#term-GeoJSON) FeatureCollection as output (rather than a Polygon for example),
generated from an input [GeoJSON](appendix.html#term-GeoJSON) Geometry.
It desires the response to be provided as [Collection Output](#proc-col-outputs), compatible with [STAC](appendix.html#term-STAC).
In this case, the input/output profiles are handled by the underlying [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) execution,
while the response profiles ([Job Status](#proc-op-status) / [Job Result](#proc-op-result)) are
specifically for Weaver as [OGC API - Processes](appendix.html#term-OGC-API-Processes) request interactions.
Note
In most situations, this level of granular control over profiles is not necessary since sensible results
are applied based on common patterns. However, they might be necessary in situations of highly overloaded
[Media-Types](appendix.html#term-Media-Types) such as [GeoJSON](appendix.html#term-GeoJSON) and [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON), or for partially compatible [API](appendix.html#term-API) or
responses between [STAC](appendix.html#term-STAC), [OGC](appendix.html#term-OGC) and [openEO](appendix.html#term-openEO) specifications. In certain cases, only a few
of them might be necessary, but it is important to reflect precisely where the [Profile](appendix.html#term-Profile) applies.
See also
Note
- Both - response[f]and- response[format]are accepted and equivalent
- response[format]provides a more explicit parameter name for better API clarity
- These parameters are optional and can be combined with input/output parameters

[Execution Steps](#id125)[](#execution-steps)
Once the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) is submitted, its status should initially switch to accepted. This effectively means that the
[Job](appendix.html#term-Job) is pending execution (task queued), but is not yet executing. When a worker retrieves it for execution, the
status will change to started for preparation steps (i.e.: allocation resources, retrieving required
parametrization details, etc.), followed by running when effectively reaching the execution step of the underlying
[Application Package](appendix.html#term-Application-Package) operation. This status will remain as such until the operation completes, either with
successful or failed status.
At any moment during [asynchronous](#proc-exec-mode) execution, the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) status can be requested using [ GET {WEAVER_URL}/processes/{processID}/jobs/{jobID} (GetStatus)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Status%2Fpaths%2F~1processes~1{process_id}~1jobs~1{job_id}%2Fget). Note that
depending on the timing at which the user executes this request and the availability of task workers, it could be
possible that the
[Job](appendix.html#term-Job)be already in
running state, or even failed in case of early problem detected.When the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) reaches its final state, multiple parameters will be adjusted in the status response to
indicate its completion, notably the completed percentage, time it finished execution and full duration. At that
moment, the requests for retrieving either error details or produced outputs become accessible. Examples are presented
in [Result](#proc-op-result) section.
