[File Reference Names](#id128)[](#file-reference-names)
When processing any of the previous [File Reference Types](#file-ref-types), the resulting name of the file after retrieval can
depend on the applicable scheme. In most cases, the file name is simply the last fragment of the path, whether it is
an URL, an [S3](appendix.html#term-S3) bucket or plainly a file directory path. The following cases are exceptions.
Changed in version 4.4: When using http(s):// references, the Content-Disposition header can be provided with filename
and/or filename* as specified by [RFC 2183](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2183.html), [RFC 5987](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5987.html) and [RFC 6266](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6266.html) specifications in order to define a
staging file name. Note that Weaver takes this name only as a suggestion as will ignore the preferred name if it
does not conform to basic naming conventions for security reasons. As a general rule of thumb, common alphanumeric
characters and separators such as dash (-), underscores (_) or dots (.) should be employed to limit
chances of errors. If none of the suggested names are valid, Weaver falls back to the typical last fragment of
the URL as file name.
Added in version 4.27: References using any scheme can refer to a Directory. Do do so, they must respect definitions in [Directory Type](package.html#cwl-dir).
When provided, all retrievable contents under that directory will be recursively staged.
When using s3:// references (or equivalent http(s):// referring to [S3](appendix.html#term-S3) bucket), the staged file names
will depend on the stored object names within the bucket. In that regard, naming conventions from [AWS](appendix.html#term-AWS) should be
respected.
When using vault://<UUID> references, the resulting file name will be obtained from the filename specified in
the Content-Disposition within the uploaded content of the multipart/form-data ([RFC 7578](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7578.html)) request.
See also
[File Vault Inputs](#id129)[](#file-vault-inputs)
See also
Refer to [Uploading File to the Vault](#vault-upload) section for general details about the [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) feature.
Stored files in the [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) can be employed as input for [Execution of a Process (Execute)](#proc-op-execute) operation using the
provided vault://<UUID> reference from the response following upload. The [Execute](#proc-op-execute)
request must also include the X-Auth-Vault header to obtain access to the file.
Warning
Avoid using the [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) HTTP location as href input. Prefer the vault://<UUID> representation.
The direct [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) HTTP location SHOULD NOT be employed as input reference to a [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) to
ensure its proper interpretation during execution. There are two main reasons for this.
Firstly, using the plain HTTP endpoint will not provide any hint to Weaver about whether the input link
is a generic remote file or one hosted in the [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault). With the lack of this information, Weaver could attempt
to download the file to retrieve it for its local [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) execution, creating unnecessary operations and wasting
bandwidth since it is already available locally. Furthermore, the [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) behaviour that deletes the file after
its download would cause it to become unavailable upon subsequent access attempts, as it could be the case during
handling and forwarding of references during intermediate [Workflow](#workflow) step operations. This could inadvertently
break the [Workflow](#workflow) execution.
Secondly, without the explicit [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) reference, Weaver cannot be aware of the necessary X-Auth-Vault
authorization needed to download it. Using the vault://<UUID> not only tells Weaver that it must forward any relevant
access token to obtain the file, but it also ensures that those tokens are not inadvertently sent to other locations.
Effectively, because the [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) can be used to temporarily host sensitive data for [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) execution,
Weaver can better control and avoid leaking the access token to irrelevant resource locations such that only the
intended [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) and specific input can access it. This is even more important in situations where multiple
[Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) references are required, to make sure each input forwards the respective access token for retrieving
its file.
When submitting the [Execute](#proc-op-execute) request, it is important to provide the X-Auth-Vault header
with additional reference to the [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) parameter when multiple files are involved. Each token should be
provided using a comma to separated them, as detailed below. When only one file refers to the [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) the
parameters can be omitted since there is no need to map between tokens and distinct vault://<UUID> entries.
POST /processes/{process_id}/execution HTTP/1.1
Host: weaver.example.com
Content-Type: application/json
X-Auth-Vault: token <access-token-1>; id=<vault-uuid-1>,token <access-token-2>; id=<vault-uuid-2>
{
"mode": "async",
"response": "document",
"inputs": {"input-1": {"href": "vault://<vault-uuid-1>"}, "input-2": {"href": "vault://<vault-uuid-2>"}},
"outputs": {"out": {"transmissionMode": "reference"}}
}
The notation ([RFC 5234](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5234.html), [RFC 7230 Section 1.2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7230.html#section-1.2)) of the X-Auth-Vault header is presented below.
X-Auth-Vault = vault-unique / vault-multi vault-unique = credentials [ BWS ";" OWS auth-param ] vault-multi = credentials BWS ";" OWS auth-param 1*( "," OWS credentials BWS ";" OWS auth-param ) credentials = auth-scheme RWS access-token auth-scheme = "token" auth-param = "id" "=" vault-id vault-id = UUID / ( DQUOTE UUID DQUOTE ) access-token = base64 base64 = <base64, see[RFC 4648 Section 4](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4648.html#section-4)> DQUOTE = <DQUOTE, see[RFC 7230 Section 1.2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7230.html#section-1.2)> UUID = <UUID, see[RFC 4122 Section 3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4122.html#section-3)> BWS = <BWS, see[RFC 7230 Section 3.2.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7230.html#section-3.2.3)> OWS = <OWS, see[RFC 7230 Section 3.2.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7230.html#section-3.2.3)> RWS = <RWS, see[RFC 7230 Section 3.2.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7230.html#section-3.2.3)>
In summary, the access token can be provided by itself by omitting the [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) UUID parameter only
if a single file is referenced across all inputs within the [Execute](#proc-op-execute) request.
Otherwise, multiple [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) references all require to specify both their respective access token
and UUID in a comma separated list.

[Collection Inputs](#id133)[](#collection-inputs)
The [Collection Input](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/21-009.html#section_collection_input) is defined by the [OGC API - Processes - Part 3: Workflows](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/21-009.html) extension. This allows to submit a
[Process Execution](#proc-op-execute) using the following [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON) structure when the targeted [Process](appendix.html#term-Process)
can make use of the resulting data sources retrieved from the referred [Collection](appendix.html#term-Collection) and processing conditions.
The collection keyword is employed to identify this type of input, in contrast to literal data and complex file
inputs respectively using value and href, as presented in the [Process Execution](#proc-op-execute)
section.
{
"inputs": {
"image-input": {
"collection": "https://example.com/collections/sentinel-2"
}
}
}
Note
More properties can be provided with the collection, such as filter, sortBy, etc.
The [OpenAPI](appendix.html#term-OpenAPI) definition in Weaver is defined with a minimal set of properties, since specific requirements
to be supported might need multiple [OGC](appendix.html#term-OGC) Testbed iterations to be established.
Also, different combinations of parameters will be supported depending on which remote [API](appendix.html#term-API) gets
interrogated to resolve the [Collection](appendix.html#term-Collection) contents. The [OGC API - Processes - Part 3: Workflows](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/21-009.html) is still under development,
and interactions with the various access points of [OGC Web API standards](https://ogcapi.ogc.org/) remains to
be evaluated in detail to further explore interoperability concerns between all [API](appendix.html#term-API) implementations.
Refer to [Examples](#proc-col-inputs-examples) for potential combinations and additional samples.
To determine which items should be retrieved from the [Collection](appendix.html#term-Collection), whether they are obtained by
[OGC API - Coverages](https://ogcapi.ogc.org/coverages/), [OGC API - Features](https://ogcapi.ogc.org/features/), [OGC API - Maps](https://ogcapi.ogc.org/maps/), [OGC API - Tiles](https://ogcapi.ogc.org/tiles/), [STAC API Specification](https://github.com/radiantearth/stac-api-spec),
or any other relevant data access mechanisms defined by the [OGC Web API standards](https://ogcapi.ogc.org/),
depends on the negotiated [Media-Types](appendix.html#term-Media-Types) required by the corresponding input
in the [Process Description](#proc-op-describe), any relevant format indication,
and capabilities offered by the server referenced with the collection [URL](appendix.html#term-URL).
For example, if a [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) input definition indicates that
it accepts [GeoJSON](appendix.html#term-GeoJSON) (application/geo+json) as its contents [Media-Type](appendix.html#term-Media-Type),
or contains a format: geojson-feature-collection indication within its schema definition,
the referenced collection would most probably need to resolve access to the data
using [OGC API - Features](https://ogcapi.ogc.org/features/) (i.e.: with request GET /collections/dataset-features/items),
to retrieve relevant [GeoJSON](appendix.html#term-GeoJSON) items as a FeatureCollection, which would then be
passed to the corresponding input of the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process).
However, depending on the capabilities of the server (e.g.: a [STAC API](https://github.com/radiantearth/stac-api-spec) instance or various extension support),
the POST /search or the POST /collections/dataset-features/search operations could be considered as well.
Alternatively, if an array of image/tiff; application=geotiff is expected by the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) input definition
and the submitted input provides a collection referring to a [STAC API](https://github.com/radiantearth/stac-api-spec) endpoint,
the [STAC Assets](https://github.com/radiantearth/stac-spec/blob/master/commons/assets.md) matching the requested [Media-Type](appendix.html#term-Media-Type) could potentially be retrieved as input for
the [Process Execution](#proc-op-execute).
Contrary to an href input where the referenced [URL](appendix.html#term-URL) (potentially pointing at a [Collection](appendix.html#term-Collection)
with predefined filtering query parameters) is directly accessed with a single request, the collection input offers
the option to the server to further negotiate and resolve the targeted [Collection](appendix.html#term-Collection) reference and the data it
contains. In some situations, such as when a very large amount of data needs to be accessed and retrieved with an
iterative paging or tiling approach, the collection input allows to automatically resolve this operation
(as supported by the server), whereas the direct href reference would only return the limited content as directly
responded by the server hosting the :term`Collection`, and potentially not reflecting the actual intent of the user
submitting the [Process Execution](#proc-op-execute). Therefore, the collection allows the resolution of more
complex data access mechanisms that cannot be resolved by a single request or operation.
In summary, the [Collection Input](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/21-009.html#section_collection_input) offers a lot of flexibility with its resolution compared to
the typical [Input Types](package.html#cwl-io-types) (i.e.: Literal, BoundingBox, Complex) that must be explicitly
specified. However, its capability to auto-resolve multiple [Media-Types](appendix.html#term-Media-Types) negotiations, formats, data structures,
data cardinality and [API](appendix.html#term-API) access mechanisms simultaneously can make its behavior hard to predict.
Hint
In order to evaluate the expected resolution of a [Collection](appendix.html#term-Collection)
prior to including it into a complex [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) or [Workflow](#workflow) execution, the [Builtin](#proc-builtin)
[ weaver.processes.builtin.collection_processor](autoapi/weaver/processes/builtin/collection_processor/index.html#module-weaver.processes.builtin.collection_processor) can be employed to test its result.
This function will be used under-the-hood whenever a
[Collection Input](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/21-009.html#section_collection_input)is specified.
Since the [Builtin Process](appendix.html#term-Builtin-Process) only performs the resolution of the collection into the corresponding
data sources for the target [Process](appendix.html#term-Process), without actually downloading the resolved [URL](appendix.html#term-URL) references,
using it can potentially help identify and avoid unintended large processing, or allow users to validate that
the defined filter (or any other below parameters) produces the appropriate data retrieval strategy for the
desired execution purpose.
See also
The [Examples](#proc-col-inputs-examples) section further demonstrates how to
apply [Collection Input](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/21-009.html#section_collection_input) and how its parameters can help produce various result combinations.
Note
Do not hesitate to [submit a new issue](https://github.com/crim-ca/weaver/issues/new/choose) if the [Collection Input](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/21-009.html#section_collection_input) resolution does not seem
to behave according to your specific use cases.

Filtering[](#filtering)
When adding a filter parameter along the collection reference, it is possible to provide filtering conditions
to limit the items to be extracted from the [Collection](appendix.html#term-Collection). See the [Examples](#proc-col-inputs-examples) for samples.
In the event that a filter contains coordinates that do not employ the
commonly employed default [CRS](appendix.html#term-CRS) of EPSG:4326 (or CRS84/CRS84h equivalents),
the filter-crs parameter can be specified to provide the applicable [CRS](appendix.html#term-CRS).
Note
Weaver will not itself interpret the filter-crs beside transforming between [URI](appendix.html#term-URI) and
common short name representations to ensure the remote [API](appendix.html#term-API) can properly resolve the intended reference.
If a filter-crs is provided, it is up to the remote [API](appendix.html#term-API) receiving it to interpret it and the
referenced coordinates within filter correctly.
If the targeted server by the collection [URL](appendix.html#term-URL) cannot resolve the [CRS](appendix.html#term-CRS), the user will need
to convert it themselves to make it appropriate according to the target server capabilities.
The filter-lang parameter can be employed to indicate which language encoding is specified in filter.
At the moment, the following languages (case-insensitive) are handled in Weaver using pygeofilter.

Note
Although there are a lot of “Common Query Language” (CQL) variations, most of them only imply minimal variations between some operations, sometimes allowing alternate or additional systax and/or operators.
Because most [OGC Web API standards](https://ogcapi.ogc.org/) rely extensively on [CQL2-JSON](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/21-065r3.html#cql2-json) or [CQL2-Text](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/21-065r3.html#cql2-text) encodings,
and that most of them have common bases that can be easily translated, all language variants
will be converted to an appropriate and equivalent CQL2-based definition, before submitting
it to the [Collection](appendix.html#term-Collection) resolution operation.
Examples[](#proc-col-inputs-examples)
The following section presents some examples of potential [Collection Input](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/21-009.html#section_collection_input) definitions that could
be used for [Process Execution](#proc-op-execute), and some explanation about their expected resolution.
The following example presents the use of a filter encoded with [CQL2-JSON](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/21-065r3.html#cql2-json), used to limit the retrieved
geometries only to [Feature](appendix.html#term-Feature) instances that intersect the specified polygon. Any [Feature](appendix.html#term-Feature) that was matched
should also be sorted in descending order of their respective id property, according to the sortBy parameter.
Furthermore, the [OGC API - Features](https://ogcapi.ogc.org/features/) resolution is requested using the format parameter. Because it is
expected from this [API](appendix.html#term-API) that a [GeoJSON](appendix.html#term-GeoJSON) FeatureCollection document would be returned,
the features input of the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) receiving this result should support application/geo+json
or a similar schema definition for this execution request to be successful. Since this [Media-Type](appendix.html#term-Media-Type)
is the default value returned by [OGC API - Features](https://ogcapi.ogc.org/features/), the type does not need to be set explicitly.
{
"inputs": {
"features": {
"collection": "https://example.com/collections/dataset-features",
"format": "ogc-feature-collection",
"filter": {
"op": "s_intersects",
"args": [
{"property": "geometry"},
{
"type": "Polygon",
"coordinates": [ [30, 10], [40, 40], [20, 40], [10, 20], [30, 10] ]
}
]
},
"filter-crs": "https://www.opengis.net/def/crs/OGC/1.3/CRS84",
"filter-lang": "cql2-json",
"sortBy": "-id"
}
}
}
The following example presents a filter encoded with [CQL2-Text](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/21-065r3.html#cql2-text), which aims to return only elements
that contain a property matching the eo:cloud_cover < 0.1 criteria from the [Collection](appendix.html#term-Collection)
named sentinel-2. In this case, the [STAC API Specification](https://github.com/radiantearth/stac-api-spec) is indicated by the format. Therefore,
[STAC Items](https://github.com/radiantearth/stac-spec/blob/master/item-spec/item-spec.md) defined under that [Collection](appendix.html#term-Collection) are expected to be considered if their properties respect
the eo:cloud_cover filter. However, the [Media-Type](appendix.html#term-Media-Type) defined by type corresponding to [Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (COG)](http://www.cogeo.org/)
is also specified, meaning that the result from the [Collection Input](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/21-009.html#section_collection_input) resolution is not
the [GeoJSON](appendix.html#term-GeoJSON) [STAC Items](https://github.com/radiantearth/stac-spec/blob/master/item-spec/item-spec.md) themselves, but the [STAC Assets](https://github.com/radiantearth/stac-spec/blob/master/commons/assets.md) they respectively contain, and that match
this GeoTIFF type.
Therefore, the definition of the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) input images should support an array of GeoTIFF images,
for this resolution to succeed, and proceed to execute the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) using them.
{
"inputs": {
"images": {
"collection": "https://example.com/collections/sentinel-2",
"format": "stac-collection",
"type": "image/tiff; application=geotiff; profile=cloud-optimized",
"filter": "properties.eo:cloud_cover < 0.1",
"filter-lang": "cql2-text"
}
}
}

[Outputs Location](#id137)[](#outputs-location)
By default, [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) results will be hosted under the endpoint configured by weaver.wps_output_url and
weaver.wps_output_path, and will be stored under directory defined by weaver.wps_output_dir setting.
Warning
Hosting of results from the file system is NOT handled by Weaver itself. The API will only report the
expected endpoints using configured weaver.wps_output_url. It is up to an alternate service or the platform
provider that serves the Weaver application to provide the external hosting and availability of files online
as desired.
Each [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) will have its specific UUID employed for all of the outputs files, logs and status in order to
avoid conflicts. Therefore, outputs will be available with the following location:
{WPS_OUTPUT_URL}/{JOB_UUID}.xml # status location
{WPS_OUTPUT_URL}/{JOB_UUID}.log # execution logs
{WPS_OUTPUT_URL}/{JOB_UUID}/{outputID}/{output.ext} # results of the job if successful
Note
Value WPS_OUTPUT_URL in above example is resolved accordingly with weaver.wps_output_url,
weaver.wps_output_path and weaver.url, as per [Configuration Settings](configuration.html#conf-settings) details.
When submitting a [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) for execution, it is possible to provide the X-WPS-Output-Context header.
This modifies the output location to be nested under the specified directory or sub-directories.
For example, providing X-WPS-Output-Context: project/test-1 will result in outputs located at:
{WPS_OUTPUT_URL}/project/test-1/{JOB_UUID}/{outputID}/{output.ext}
Note
Values provided by X-WPS-Output-Context can only contain alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores and path separators
that will result in a valid directory and [URL](appendix.html#term-URL) locations. The path is assumed relative by design to be
resolved under the [WPS](appendix.html#term-WPS) output directory, and will therefore reject any . or .. path references.
The path also CANNOT start by /. In such cases, an HTTP error will be immediately raised indicating
the symbols that where rejected when detected within X-WPS-Output-Context header.
If desired, parameter weaver.wps_output_context can also be defined in the [Configuration Settings](configuration.html#conf-settings) in order to employ
a default directory location nested under weaver.wps_output_dir when X-WPS-Output-Context header is omitted
from the request. By default, this parameter is not defined (empty) in order to store [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) results directly under
the configured [WPS](appendix.html#term-WPS) output directory.
Note
Header X-WPS-Output-Context is ignored when using S3 buckets for output location since they are stored
individually per [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) UUID, and hold no relevant context location. See also [Configuration of AWS S3 Buckets](configuration.html#conf-s3-buckets).
Changed in version 4.3: Addition of the X-WPS-Output-Context header.
[Notification Subscribers](#id138)[](#notification-subscribers)
When submitting a [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) for execution, it is possible to provide the notification_email field.
Doing so will tell Weaver to send an email to the specified address with successful or failure details
upon [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) completion. The format of the email is configurable from [weaver.ini.example](../../../config/weaver.ini.example) file with
email-specific settings (see: [Email Configuration](configuration.html#weaver-wps-email)).
Alternatively to notification_email, the subscribers field of the [API](appendix.html#term-API) can be employed during [Job](appendix.html#term-Job)
submission. Using this field will take precedence over notification_email for corresponding email and status
combinations. The [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) subscribers allow more fined-grained control over which emails will be sent for
the various combinations of [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) status milestones.
Furthermore, subscribers allow specifying URLs where HTTP(S) callback requests (i.e.: webhooks) will be sent with
the [Job Status](#proc-op-status) or [Job Results](#proc-op-result) contents directly in [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON) format.
This allows users and/or servers to directly receive the necessary details using a push-notification mechanism instead
of the polling-based method on the [Job Status](#proc-op-status) endpoint otherwise required to obtain updated
[Job](appendix.html#term-Job) details.
See also
Refer to the [OpenAPI Documentation](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html) of the [ POST {WEAVER_URL}/processes/{processID}/execution (Execute)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Processes/paths/~1processes~1{process_id}~1execution/post) request for all available
subscribers properties.[Job Management](#id139)[](#job-management)
This section presents capabilities related to [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) management.
The endpoints and related operations are defined in a mixture of [OGC API - Processes](https://github.com/opengeospatial/ogcapi-processes) Core requirements,
some official extensions, and further Weaver-specific capabilities.
See also
[Submitting a Job Creation](#id140)[](#submitting-a-job-creation)
Important
All concepts introduced in the [Execution of a Process](#proc-op-execute) also apply in this section.
Consider reading the subsections for more specific details.
This section will only cover additional concepts and parameters applicable only for this feature.
Rather than using the [ POST {WEAVER_URL}/processes/{processID}/execution (Execute)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Processes/paths/~1processes~1{process_id}~1execution/post) request, the
[request can be used to submit a](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Jobs/paths/~1jobs/post)
POST {WEAVER_URL}/jobs (Create)[Job](appendix.html#term-Job). When doing so, all parameters typically required for
[Process](appendix.html#term-Process)execution must also be provided, including any relevant
[Execution Body](#proc-exec-body)contents (
[I/O](appendix.html#term-I-O)), the desired
[Execution Mode](#proc-exec-mode), and the
[Execution Results](#proc-exec-results)options. However, an additional
process [URL](appendix.html#term-URL)in the request body is required, to indicate which
[Process](appendix.html#term-Process)should be executed by the
[Job](appendix.html#term-Job).
The [ POST {WEAVER_URL}/jobs (Create)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Jobs/paths/~1jobs/post) operation allows interoperability alignement with other execution strategies, such as defined
by the
[openEO API Profiles](https://openeo.org/documentation/1.0/developers/profiles/api.html)and the
[OGC Testbed-20 - GeoDataCubes (GDC) API Profile](https://docs.ogc.org/per/24-035.html). It also opens the door for advanced
[Workflow](appendix.html#term-Workflow)definitions from a common
[Job](appendix.html#term-Job)endpoint interface, as described by the
[OGC API - Processes - Part 4: Job Management](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/24-051.html)extension.
Furthermore, an optional "status": "create" request body parameter can be supplied to indicate to the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job)
that it should remain in pending state, until a later [Job Execution Trigger](#proc-op-job-trigger) is performed
to start its execution. This allows the user to apply any desired [Job Updates](#proc-op-job-update) or reviewing
the resolved [Job Inputs](#proc-op-job-inputs) prior to submitting the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job). This acts in contrast to
the Core [ POST {WEAVER_URL}/processes/{processID}/execution (Execute)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Processes/paths/~1processes~1{process_id}~1execution/post) operation that immediately places the
[Job](appendix.html#term-Job)in queue, locking it from any update.
[Updating a Job](#id141)[](#updating-a-job)
The [ PATCH {WEAVER_URL}/jobs/{jobID} (Update)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Jobs/paths/~1jobs~1{job_id}/patch) request allows updating the
[Job](appendix.html#term-Job)and its underlying parameters prior to execution. For this reason, it has for pre-requirement to be in
created [Job Status](#proc-op-job-status), such that it is pending a
[Job Execution Trigger](#proc-op-job-trigger)before being sent to the worker execution queue. For any other
status than created, attempts to modify the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job)will return an HTTP 423 Locked error response.
Potential parameters that can be updated are:
- Submitted - [Process](appendix.html#term-Process)- inputs
- Desired - outputsformats and representations, as per- [Execution Results](#proc-exec-results)
- Applicable - headers,- responseand- modeoptions as per- [Execution Mode](#proc-exec-mode)
- Additional metadata such as a custom - [Job](appendix.html#term-Job)- title
After updating the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job), the [Job Status](#proc-op-job-status) and [Job Inputs](#proc-op-job-inputs)
operations can further be performed to review the pending [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) state. Using all those operations allows the
user to iteratively adjust the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) until it is ready for execution, for which
the [Job Execution Trigger](#proc-op-job-trigger) would then be employed.
[Triggering Job Execution](#id142)[](#triggering-job-execution)
The [ POST {WEAVER_URL}/jobs{jobID}/results (Trigger)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Jobs/paths/~1jobs~1{job_id}~1results/post) request allows submitting a pending
[Job](appendix.html#term-Job)to the worker execution queue. Once performed, the typical
[Monitoring a Job Execution (GetStatus)](#proc-op-monitor)operation can be employed, until eventual success or failure of the
[Job](appendix.html#term-Job).
If the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) was already submitted, is already in queue, is actively running, or already finished execution,
this operation will return a HTTP 423 Locked error response.
[Monitoring a Job Execution (GetStatus)](#id143)[](#monitoring-a-job-execution-getstatus)
Monitoring the execution of a [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) consists of polling the status Location provided from the
[Execute](#proc-op-execute) or [Trigger](#proc-op-job-trigger) operation and verifying the
indicated status for the expected result.
The status can correspond to any of the value defined by [ weaver.status.Status](autoapi/weaver/status/index.html#weaver.status.Status)
accordingly to the internal state of the workers processing their execution, and the
negotiated
[Alternate Job Status](#proc-op-job-status-alt)representation.
When targeting a [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) submitted to a Weaver instance, monitoring is usually accomplished through
the [OGC API - Processes](appendix.html#term-OGC-API-Processes) endpoint using [ GET {WEAVER_URL}/processes/{processID}/jobs/{jobID} (GetStatus)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Status%2Fpaths%2F~1processes~1{process_id}~1jobs~1{job_id}%2Fget), which will return a
[JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON)body. Alternatively, the
[XML](appendix.html#term-XML)status location document returned by the
[WPS Endpoint](#wps-endpoint)could also be employed to monitor the execution.
In general, both endpoints should be interchangeable, using below mapping. The [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) monitoring process
keeps both contents equivalent according to their standard. For convenience, requesting the [execute](cli.html#weaver-execute) with
Accept: <content-type> header corresponding to either [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON) or [XML](appendix.html#term-XML) should redirect to the response
of the relevant endpoint, regardless of where the original request was submitted. Otherwise, the default contents
format is employed according to the chosen location.

[Alternate Job Status](#id144)[](#alternate-job-status)
In order to support alternate [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) status representations, the following approaches can be used when performing
the [ GET {WEAVER_URL}/processes/{processID}/jobs/{jobID} (GetStatus)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Status%2Fpaths%2F~1processes~1{process_id}~1jobs~1{job_id}%2Fget) request.
- Specify either a - profileor- schemaquery parameter (e.g.:- /jobs/{jobID}?profile=openeo).
- Specify a - profileparameter within the- Acceptheader (e.g.:- Accept: application/json; profile=openeo).
Using the [openEO](https://openeo.org/) profile for example, will allow returning status values that are appropriate
as per the [openEO API Profiles](https://openeo.org/documentation/1.0/developers/profiles/api.html) definition.
When performing [Job Status](#proc-op-job-status) requests, the received response should
contain a Content-Schema header indicating which of the applied profile is being represented.
This header is employed because multiple Content-Type: application/json headers are applicable
across multiple [API](appendix.html#term-API) implementations and status representations.

[Job Outputs](#id146)[](#job-outputs)
Note
This endpoint is a Weaver-specific implementation provided for convenience.
For the [OGC API - Processes](appendix.html#term-OGC-API-Processes) compliant endpoint, refer to [Job Results](#proc-op-job-results).
In the case of successful [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) execution, the outputs can be retrieved with [ GET {WEAVER_URL}/jobs/{jobID}/outputs (Outputs)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/outputs/paths/~1jobs~1{job_id}~1outputs/get) request to list
each corresponding output
id with the generated file reference URL. Keep in mind that the purpose of those URLs are
only to fetch the results (not persistent storage), and could therefore be purged after some reasonable amount of time.
The format should be similar to the following example, with minor variations according to [Configuration](index.html#configuration)parameters for the base
[WPS](appendix.html#term-WPS)output location:
{
"outputs": [
{
"id": "output-file",
"href": "https://example.com/wpsoutputs/f93a15be-6e16-11ea-b667-08002752172a/output_netcdf.nc",
"type": "application/x-netcdf"
},
{
"id": "output-data",
"value": 3.1416
}
]
}
The [Job Outputs](#proc-op-job-outputs) endpoint can receive additional query parameters,
such as schema=OGC+strict (see [ weaver.processes.constants.JobInputsOutputsSchema](autoapi/weaver/processes/constants/index.html#weaver.processes.constants.JobInputsOutputsSchema) for other values),
which allows it to return contents formatted slightly differently, to imitate the
[JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON)mapping representation (rather than the array) used by the
[Execution Results](#proc-exec-results)endpoint as if
response=document was specified
during submission of the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process)execution. However, this
[JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON)mapping will still employ a nested
outputs property, as presented below.{
"outputs": {
"output-file": {
"href": "https://example.com/wpsoutputs/f93a15be-6e16-11ea-b667-08002752172a/output_netcdf.nc",
"type": "application/x-netcdf"
},
"output-data": 3.1416
}
}
Because these responses nests the results under outputs (in contrast to [Job Results](#proc-op-job-results)
returning {outputID} directly at the root), other information can be returned, such as relevant links
with references to [Job Inputs](#proc-op-job-inputs), [Job Logs](#proc-op-job-logs), [Job Status](#proc-op-status),
or the source [Process Description](#proc-op-describe) that produced returned [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) outputs.
In the event of a [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) executed with response=document or Prefer: return=minimal, the contents
of [Job Results](#proc-op-job-results) will be very similar to the above [Output Mapping](#job-outputs-mapping) contents,
but with respective {outputID} returned directly at the root, instead of nesting them under outputs.
On the other hand, a [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) submitted with response=raw, Prefer: return=representation or other
combinations of Accept headers and transmissionMode parameters, can produce
many alternative content variations (see [Execution Results](#proc-exec-results)) to respect [OGC](appendix.html#term-OGC) compliance requirements.
The structure of contents received from [Job Results](#proc-op-job-results) responses can also surprisingly vary according to
the number of requested outputs [[1]](#outn), the submitted request parameters, and the alternative [Media-Type](appendix.html#term-Media-Type),
schema or literal data supported by each respective output.
For this reason, the [Job Outputs](#proc-op-job-outputs) endpoint will always provide all data and links in the
response body using the minimal representation as shown by above [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON) examples,
no matter which request parameters where originally submitted to execute the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job).
In other words, the contents of a complex [File Reference](#file-ref-types) (such as the “[ output_netcdf.nc](#job-outputs-mapping)”)
will never be directly returned inline/by-value in the
[JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON)response when using the
[Job Outputs](#proc-op-job-outputs)endpoint, and will always use the
document/minimal file link. Similarly, a literal data value will never be
returned by link reference, nor be returned directly as the response contents. An output of literal data will
always have its value included inline in the [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON)document. This behavior is performed to offer a simplified data access mechanism without having to deal will all possible combinations of data representations potentially returned by
[Execution Results](#proc-exec-results).
[Job Results](#id147)[](#job-results)
This corresponds to the [OGC API - Processes](appendix.html#term-OGC-API-Processes) compliant endpoint, using the GET {WEAVER_URL}/jobs/{jobID}/results (Results) request.
Contrary to [Job Outputs](#proc-op-job-outputs), where the [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON) document representation is always enforced,
this endpoint will respond according to the submitted [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) parameters.
See also
This section presents examples of the most typical result combinations.
For an exhaustive list of expected content results and resolution behaviors,
according to submitted execution parameters, refer to the [Execution Results](#proc-exec-results) section.
In the event of a [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) executed with response=document or Prefer: return=minimal with multiple outputs,
the contents will typically be a [JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON) mapping representation, where each requested {outputID} can be
found either as value or reference, accordingly to how they were requested or resolved according
to [Execution Results](#proc-exec-results). An example of such results is presented below.
{
"output-file": {
"href": "https://example.com/wpsoutputs/f93a15be-6e16-11ea-b667-08002752172a/output_netcdf.nc",
"type": "application/x-netcdf"
},
"output-data": 3.1416
}
Note
The {outputID} are returned at the root of the contents using this representation,
contrary to the [Job Outputs](#proc-op-job-outputs) endpoint that nests them under outputs.
When a [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) is executed with response=raw, or when the requested outputs [[1]](#outn) consisted only of
a single {outputID}, the returned data will directly
be the contents of the produced file, or literal value, as applicable according to the schema definition of the
corresponding output in the [Process Description](#proc-op-describe).
The following result will be obtained if any of the following conditions are encountered:
- The result is a complex - [File Reference](#file-ref-types)and the- Prefer: return=representationheader was used
- The result is a complex - [File Reference](#file-ref-types)and the- transmissionMode: valueparameter was used
- The result is a literal data type, whether or not - Prefer/- transmissionModewere specified with above values.
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Host: weaver.example.com
Content-ID: <output@f93a15be-6e16-11ea-b667-08002752172a>
Content-Type: application/x-netcdf
<netcdf data>
The following result will be obtained if any of the following conditions are encountered:
- The result is a complex - [File Reference](#file-ref-types)and the- Prefer: return=minimalheader was used
- The result is a complex - [File Reference](#file-ref-types)and the- transmissionMode: referenceparameter was used
- The result is a literal data type, and any above - Prefer/- transmissionModevalue is explicitly requested.
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
Host: weaver.example.com
Content-Length: 0
Content-Type: application/x-netcdf
Content-ID: <output@f93a15be-6e16-11ea-b667-08002752172a>
Content-Location: https://example.com/wpsoutputs/f93a15be-6e16-11ea-b667-08002752172a/output/output_netcdf.nc
Link: <https://example.com/wpsoutputs/f93a15be-6e16-11ea-b667-08002752172a/output/output_netcdf.nc>; rel="output"; type="application/x-netcdf"
When results are resolved as transmissionMode: reference, either using Prefer: return=minimal
or response: raw parameters, leading to the creation of a [File Reference](#file-ref-types) link
directly returned as above (rather than embedded in a [Document Result](#job-results-document-minimal)),
the generated reference will be reported using a HTTP Link header, for each applicable output, in order to fulfill
[OGC API - Processes](appendix.html#term-OGC-API-Processes) v1.0 [Requirement 30](https://docs.ogc.org/is/18-062r2/18-062r2.html#req_core_process-execute-sync-raw-ref).
However, given that such Link headers can result into conflicting rel: {outputID} with other Link
entries found in the response, and that they require additional parsing of the value to extract the [URL](appendix.html#term-URL),
a combination of Content-ID, Content-Type and Content-Location will also be provided.
Note
For cases where an output would represent an array of [File References](#file-ref-types), returned Link
headers for each of these links will employ rel: "{outputID}.{index}" with their respective index from
the array.
To respect [RFC 2392](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2392.html) definitions, Content-ID will use pattern <{outputID}@{jobID}> as unique identifier,
and <{outputID}.{index}@{jobID}> in the case of an array of [File References](#file-ref-types).
When the number of requested outputs [[1]](#outn) is more than one, the obtained response will depend
on the negotiated Accept content header and the data/link resolution of each output.
- If all outputs are - [File References](#file-ref-types)and no- Acceptheader was specified, a no-content response with a- Linkfor each output similarly to the above- [Results for a single output returned directly by reference](#job-results-raw-single-ref)is returned.
- If a - response=documentor- Prefer: return=minimalresolution is requested, outputs are embedded in the- [Document Result](#job-results-document-minimal)contents.
- If either - multipartcontents (- [RFC 2046 Section 5.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2046.html#section-5.1)) are explicitly requested by- Acceptheader, or that the above cases were not encountered, a multipart content response as shown below is returned- [[3]](#resctypemulti).
The resolution of the nested outputs within each boundary, either by value or reference, will resolve for each respective output according to the same rule conditions specified above for single output.
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Host: weaver.example.com
Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=43003e2f205a180ace9cd34d98f911ff
--43003e2f205a180ace9cd34d98f911ff
Content-Type: application/x-netcdf
Content-ID: <output-file@f93a15be-6e16-11ea-b667-08002752172a>
Content-Location: https://example.com/wpsoutputs/f93a15be-6e16-11ea-b667-08002752172a/output-file/output_netcdf.nc
--43003e2f205a180ace9cd34d98f911ff
Content-Type: text/plain
Content-ID: <output-data@f93a15be-6e16-11ea-b667-08002752172a>
3.1416
--43003e2f205a180ace9cd34d98f911ff--
Note that, in the above response, the Content-Location is used for the output-file, whereas the data
is directly returned for the output-data. This is based on Weaver auto-resolving transmissionMode: reference
for a [File Reference](#file-ref-types) result, while using transmissionMode: value by default for literal
data types. This also assumes that response: raw was requested, and that no transmissionMode were specified.
If transmissionMode: value under output-file in the requested outputs [[1]](#outn) was used
(or alternatively, if Prefer: return=representation was specified),
the data of the file would be directly included inline within the response instead of using Content-Location,
similarly to the [Single Output Value](#job-results-raw-single-data) example,
but with its contents nested within its respective boundaries for the corresponding Content-ID.
[Job Single Output Retrieval](#id148)[](#job-single-output-retrieval)
Added in version 6.12.0.
When only one output is needed, and following a successful [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) execution,
the desired result can be obtained directly without requesting the whole result set, using:
GET /jobs/{jobID}/results/{outputID} HTTP/1.1
Host: weaver.example.com
Equivalent [Process](appendix.html#term-Process)-scoped and [Provider](appendix.html#term-Provider)-scoped prefixes can be used in the same way, as described
in [Obtaining Job Details and Metadata](#proc-op-job-detail). For convenience, the ../outputs/{outputID} endpoint can also be used as an alias
to the above ../results/{outputID} endpoint.
When the selected {outputID} corresponds to an array result, a specific element can be obtained with:
GET /jobs/{jobID}/results/{outputID}/{index} HTTP/1.1
Host: weaver.example.com
This indexed route is therefore the same single-output retrieval strategy, but with an additional selector
applied on the array value for convenience. It can also be employed to convert only a single element of the array
to another supported [Media-Type](appendix.html#term-Media-Type), without triggering conversion for the entire array.
Submitting a request to the {index} endpoint for an {outputID} that does not correspond to an array will
return an HTTP error response. Using the endpoint without {index} will return the whole array as a single output,
or as the output itself it is not an array.
The representation of returned content for single-output retrieval follows similar
[Resolution Resolution](#proc-exec-results) and [Content Negotiation](#proc-content-negotiation) principles
and parameters to their multi-output counterparts. However, any indication of >1 considerations are not applicable
in this case, since only one output is requested. Similarly, the semantics of the negotiated formats apply to the
specifically requested single output directly, rather than to a response containing multiple outputs with
different formats. Therefore, certain formats might not be applicable to certain cases.
Warning
Although /jobs/{jobID}/results/{outputID} and /jobs/{jobID}/results/{outputID}/{index} can be
used to obtain distinct subsets of “outputs”, they all refer to the same [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) outputID.
Therefore, the [Content Negotiation](#proc-content-negotiation) is performed the same way. For example, requesting a
GeoTIFF [Media-Type](appendix.html#term-Media-Type) for an output that supports it would return either the whole array, each item a
distinct GeoTIFF, or only the specific one by {index}. It will NOT create a “container”-like
representation of that GeoTIFF (e.g.: by stacking bands).
That is different from the [Content Negotiation](#proc-content-negotiation) performed for the /jobs/{jobID}/results endpoint
itself, which MAY perform some sort of packaging of a [Multiple Outputs](#proc-multi-outputs) representation of the whole result
set, for example by returning a ZIP representation instead of the default
[JSON Job Results](#job-results-document-minimal) document.

inputs that were submitted,
as well as the requested outputs [[1]](#outn)to retrieve any relevant
transmissionMode, format, etc.
parameters that where specified during submission of the [Execution Body](#proc-exec-body), and any other relevant
headers
that can affect the [Execution Mode](#proc-exec-mode)and

[Job Exceptions](#id150)[](#job-exceptions)
In situations where the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) resulted into failed status, the [ GET {WEAVER_URL}/processes/{processID}/jobs/{jobID}/exceptions (GetLogs)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Logs%2Fpaths%2F~1processes~1%7Bprocess_id%7D~1jobs~1%7Bjob_id%7D~1logs%2Fget) can be used to retrieve
the potential cause of failure, by capturing any raised exception. Below is an example of such exception details.
[
"builtins.Exception: Could not read status document after 5 retries. Giving up."
]
The returned exception are often better understood when compared against, or in conjunction with, the logs that provide details over each step of the operation.
[Job Logs](#id151)[](#job-logs)
Any [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) executed by Weaver will provide minimal information log, such as operation setup, the moment
when it started execution and latest status. The extent of other log entries will more often than not depend on the
verbosity of the underlying process being executed. When executing an [Application Package](package.html#id1), Weaver tries as
best as possible to collect standard output and error steams to report them through log and exception lists.
Since Weaver can only report as much details as provided by the running application, it is recommended by
[Application Package](appendix.html#term-Application-Package) implementers to provide progressive status updates when developing their package
in order to help understand problematic steps in event of process execution failures. In the case of remote [WPS](appendix.html#term-WPS)
processes monitored by Weaver for example, this means gradually reporting process status updates
(e.g.: calling WPSResponse.update_status if you are using [PyWPS](https://github.com/geopython/pywps/), see: [Progress and Status Report](https://pywps.readthedocs.io/en/master/process.html#progress-and-status-report)), while using print
and/or logging operation for scripts or [Docker](appendix.html#term-Docker) images executed through [CWL](appendix.html#term-CWL) CommandLineTool.
Note
[Job](appendix.html#term-Job) logs and exceptions are a Weaver-specific implementation.
They are not part of traditional [OGC API - Processes](https://github.com/opengeospatial/ogcapi-processes).
A minimalistic example of logging output is presented below. This can be retrieved using [ GET {WEAVER_URL}/processes/{processID}/jobs/{jobID}/logs (GetLogs)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Logs%2Fpaths%2F~1processes~1%7Bprocess_id%7D~1jobs~1%7Bjob_id%7D~1logs%2Fget) request, at any
moment during
[Job](appendix.html#term-Job)execution (with logs up to that point in time) or after its completion (for full output). Note again that the more the
[Process](appendix.html#term-Process)is verbose, the more tracking will be provided here.

[Job Provenance](#id152)[](#job-provenance)
Added in version 6.1.
The provenance endpoints allow to obtain [W3C](appendix.html#term-W3C) [PROV](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-overview/) metadata from a successfully completed [Job](appendix.html#term-Job)
using various representations. This provenance information can help identify traceability information such as the input
data sources, validate output checksums, and understand all internal [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) data transformations that were
involved within an executed [Workflow](appendix.html#term-Workflow).
The [PROV](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-overview/) metadata consists of information records about entities, activities, and people involved in producing a
piece of data or thing [[^]](https://www.w3.org/TR/2013/REC-prov-dm-20130430/#dfn-provenance), which can be used to form assessments about its quality, reliability or
trustworthiness.
The provenance endpoints are provided in alignment with the [OGC API - Processes - Part 4: Job Management](https://docs.ogc.org/DRAFTS/24-051.html) provenance class requirement.
However, Weaver also provides additional functionalities in comparison to the minimal requirements from the
[OGC](appendix.html#term-OGC) specification.

[Content Negotiation](#id154)[](#content-negotiation)
Content negotiation can be performed using multiple query parameters and headers when submitting a [Job](appendix.html#term-Job)
execution request, when retrieving the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) results, or when inspecting the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) description
to execute. Content negotiation also happens within the submitted [Execution Body](#proc-exec-body) contents for respective

[Profile Resolution Order](#id156)[](#profile-resolution-order)
Possible locations where [Profile](appendix.html#term-Profile) can be specified are, in order of precedence:
- profilequery parameter.
- Accept-Profileheader directly providing the profile- [URI](appendix.html#term-URI).
- Accept- [Media-Type](appendix.html#term-Media-Type)with a- profileparameter.
- Preferheader including a- profileparameter.
- Linkheader including a link relation named- profile.
See also
- Implementation of the resolution order in Weaver is provided in - weaver.utils.get_response_profile()
Note
The precedence requirement is mostly predominant regarding the use of a profile query parameter in contrast
to any other header variant. This is simply due to the fact that inserting a query parameter is the simplest
method to provide a [Profile](appendix.html#term-Profile), especially in the case of web browsers where headers are more
complicated to include in the request. Therefore, combining multiple headers approaches simultaneously with
distinct [Profile](appendix.html#term-Profile) values is considered undefined or random behavior by referenced standards.
In Weaver, the prioritization strategy is defined in terms of most explicit and most common header names to
least probable ones regarding where the [Profile](appendix.html#term-Profile) is potentially located. Another consideration for the order
is the “strictness requirement” aspect of each header. The Accept header imposes a strict refusal of the
request (406 Not Acceptable) if the [Profile](appendix.html#term-Profile) is not supported for a given endpoint, while the Prefer
header is more relaxed and fulfillment is optional. The server is allowed to ignore the failing Prefer condition
and respond successfully, unless handling=strict ([RFC 7240 Section 4.4](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7240.html#section-4.4)) is indicated.
The Link header is placed last, to potentially allow Prefer priority if a given [Profile](appendix.html#term-Profile) can be
respected, and revert back to [Profile](appendix.html#term-Profile) specified by Link otherwise. This allows the simultaneous submission
of Prefer: profile="{URI}" and Link: <{URI}>; rel=profile headers in a request with flexible outcomes between
clients and servers supporting different [Profile](appendix.html#term-Profile) interoperability. In this case, the Link header can be
used to provide a fallback if the [Profile](appendix.html#term-Profile) in Prefer header cannot not be respected or resolved by the server
for the given request context. Fulfilling the [Profile](appendix.html#term-Profile) in Link header is “more important” in this fallback
scenario, but still NOT mandatory, contrary to the Accept and Accept-Profile headers that must be respected
to fulfill the request successfully.
[Transformed Output Considerations](#id157)[](#transformed-output-considerations)
Added in version 6.12.0.
From a client perspective, output content-negotiation produced directly by an originally deployed [Process](appendix.html#term-Process)
definition or through an alternate format [Transform](appendix.html#term-Transform) uses the same mechanisms. All supported [Media-Types](appendix.html#term-Media-Types)
by a given [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) output are described in the same manner. However, the underlying [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) definition
composes that set of supported formats by combining the native formats declared in the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) definition
(which may come from the declared [Deployment Metadata](#proc-op-deploy) and/or [Application Package](appendix.html#term-Application-Package))
and any additional transformation formats builtin within Weaver.
Additional [Transform](appendix.html#term-Transform) formats can extend those declared formats for simple result retrieval when a compatible
conversion is available. If a [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) already defines support of a given [Media-Types](appendix.html#term-Media-Types) at deployment time,
this format should be natively managed by the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) rather than the [Transform](appendix.html#term-Transform) utilities.
Retrieval methods remain unchanged, including [Job Results](#proc-op-job-results) for complete result sets and
[Job Single Output Retrieval](#proc-op-job-results-single) for direct per-output access, with either variant.
The available alternative [Transform](appendix.html#term-Transform) formats are defined in [ weaver.transform](autoapi/weaver/transform/index.html#module-weaver.transform). They are selected on a
per-output basis based on the applicable output constrains inherited from the original
[Process](appendix.html#term-Process)definition, and by cases where compatible
[Transform](appendix.html#term-Transform)combinations can be established, if not already provided. For example, a
[Process](appendix.html#term-Process)that produces a
[JSON](appendix.html#term-JSON)output may automatically support additional transformations to corresponding CSV,
[XML](appendix.html#term-XML)and
[YAML](appendix.html#term-YAML)representations. However, it is to be noted that these transformations are performed literally and meant to be relatively low-level operations, meaning that advanced semantic interpretation and metadata of the formats will often not be considered. For advanced transformations including domain-specific interpretation of the data, it is recommended to implement them directly with a dedicated and reusable
[Process](appendix.html#term-Process)definition, which can be chained within a
[Workflow](#proc-workflow).
[Uploading File to the Vault](#id158)[](#uploading-file-to-the-vault)
The [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) is available as secured storage for uploading files to be employed later for [Process](appendix.html#term-Process)
execution (see also [File Vault Inputs](#file-vault-inputs)).
Note
The [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) is a specific feature of Weaver. Other [ADES](appendix.html#term-ADES), [EMS](appendix.html#term-EMS) and [OGC API - Processes](appendix.html#term-OGC-API-Processes)
servers are not expected to provide this endpoint nor support the vault://<UUID> reference format.
See also
Refer to [Configuration of File Vault](configuration.html#conf-vault) for applicable settings for this feature.
When upload succeeds, the response will return a [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) UUID and an access_token to access the file.
Uploaded files cannot be accessed unless the proper credentials are provided. Requests toward the [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) should
therefore include a X-Auth-Vault: token {access_token] header in combination to the provided [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) UUID in
the request path to retrieve the file contents. The upload response will also include a file_href field formatted
with a vault://<UUID> reference to be used for [File Vault Inputs](#file-vault-inputs), as well as a Content-Location header of the
contextual [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) endpoint for that file.
Download of the file is accomplished using the [Vault File Download (GET)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Vault/paths/~1vault~1{file_id}/get) request.
In order to either obtain the file metadata without downloading it, or simply to validate its existence,
the [Vault File Details (HEAD)](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Vault/paths/~1vault~1{file_id}/head) request can be used. This HEAD request can be queried any number of times without affecting
the file from the [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault). For both HTTP methods, the X-Auth-Vault header is required.
Note
The [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) acts only as temporary file storage. For this reason, once the file has been downloaded, it is
immediately deleted. Download can only occur once. It is assumed that the resource that must employ it will have
created a local copy from the download and the [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) doesn’t require to preserve it anymore. This behaviour
intends to limit the duration for which potentially sensitive data remains available in the [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) as well
as performing cleanup to limit storage space.
Using the [Weaver CLI or Python client](cli.html#cli), it is possible to upload local files automatically to the
[Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) of a remote Weaver server. This can help users host their local file for remote [Process](appendix.html#term-Process)
execution. By default, the [Weaver CLI and Client](cli.html#cli) will automatically convert any local file path provided as execution input into
a vault://<UUID> reference to make use of the [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) self-hosting from the target Weaver instance. It will also
update the provided inputs or execution body to apply any transformed vault://<UUID> references transparently. This will
allow the executed [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) to securely retrieve the files using [File Vault Inputs](#file-vault-inputs) behaviour. Transmission
of any required authorization headers is also handled automatically when using this approach.
It is also possible to manually provide vault://<UUID> references or endpoints if those were uploaded beforehand using
the upload operation, but the user must also generate the X-Auth-Vault header manually in such case.
See also
Section [File Vault Inputs](#file-vault-inputs) provides more details about the format of X-Auth-Vault for submission
of multiple inputs.
In order to manually upload files, the below code snippet can be employed.
import json
import requests
PATH = "/path/to/local/file.json"
with open(PATH, "w", encoding="utf-8") as file:
json.dump({"input": "data"}, file)
# provide the desired name and format Media-Type
files = {
"file": (
"desired-name.json",
open(PATH, mode="r", encoding="utf-8"), # pylint: disable=R1732
"application/json; charset=UTF-8"
)
}
requests.post("https://weaver.example.com/vault", files=files, timeout=5)
This should automatically generate a similar request to the result below.
POST /vault HTTP/1.1
Host: weaver.example.com
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=43003e2f205a180ace9cd34d98f911ff
Content-Length: 202
--43003e2f205a180ace9cd34d98f911ff
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="desired-name.json"
Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8
{"input": "data"}
--43003e2f205a180ace9cd34d98f911ff--
Warning
When providing literal HTTP request contents as above, make sure to employ CRLF instead of plain LF for
separating the data using the boundary. Also, make sure to omit any additional LF between the data and each
boundary if this could impact parsing of the data itself (e.g.: as in the case of non-text readable base64 data)
to avoid modifying the file contents during upload. Some additional newlines are presented in the above example
only for readability purpose. It is recommended to use utilities like the Python example or
the [Weaver CLI](cli.html#cli) so avoid such issues during request content generation.
Please refer to [RFC 7578 Section 4.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7578.html#section-4.1) for more details regarding multipart content separators.
Note that the Content-Type embedded within the multipart content in the above example (not to be confused with the
actual Content-Type header of the request for uploading the file) can be important if the destination input of
the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) that will consume that [Vault](appendix.html#term-Vault) file for execution must provide a specific choice of
Media-Type if multiple are supported. This value could be employed to generate the explicit format portion of the
input, in case it cannot be resolved automatically from the file contents, or unless it is explicitly provided once
again for that input within the [Execute](#proc-op-execute) request body.
[WPS Endpoint](#id159)[](#wps-endpoint)
This endpoint is available if weaver.wps setting was enabled (true by default).
The specific location where [WPS](appendix.html#term-WPS) requests it will be accessible depends on the resolution
of relevant [Configuration Settings](configuration.html#conf-settings), namely weaver.wps_path and weaver.wps_url.
Details regarding contents for each request is provided in schemas under [WPS Endpoint Requests](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/WPS).
Note
Using the [WPS](appendix.html#term-WPS) endpoint allows fewer control over functionalities than the
corresponding [OGC API - Processes](appendix.html#term-OGC-API-Processes) ([WPS-REST](appendix.html#term-WPS-REST)) endpoints since it is the preceding standard.
[Special Weaver EMS use-cases](#id160)[](#special-weaver-ems-use-cases)
This section highlight the additional behaviour available only through an [EMS](appendix.html#term-EMS)-configured Weaver instance.
Some other points are already described in other sections, but are briefly indicated here for conciseness.
[ADES dispatching using Data Sources](#id161)[](#ades-dispatching-using-data-sources)
When using either the [EMS](appendix.html#term-EMS) or [HYBRID](appendix.html#term-HYBRID) [[18]](#notedatasource) configurations, [Process](appendix.html#term-Process)
executions are dispatched to the relevant [ADES](appendix.html#term-ADES) or another [HYBRID](appendix.html#term-HYBRID) server supporting
[Process Deployment](#proc-op-deploy)
when inputs are matched against one of the configured [Data Source](appendix.html#term-Data-Source). Minimal implementations
of [OGC API - Processes](appendix.html#term-OGC-API-Processes) can also work as external [Provider](appendix.html#term-Provider) where to dispatch executions, but in
the case of core implementations, the [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) should be already available since it cannot be deployed.
In more details, when an [Execute](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Processes/paths/~1processes~1{process_id}~1execution/post) request is received, Weaver will analyse any file references in the
specified inputs and try to match them against specified [Data Source](appendix.html#term-Data-Source) configuration. When a match is found
and that the corresponding [File Reference Types](#file-ref-types) indicates that the reference is located remotely in a known
[Data Source](appendix.html#term-Data-Source) provider that should take care of its processing, Weaver will attempt to [Deploy](https://pavics-weaver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#tag/Processes%2Fpaths%2F~1processes%2Fpost)
the targeted [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) (and the underlying [Application Package](appendix.html#term-Application-Package)) followed by its remote execution.
It will then monitor the [Job](appendix.html#term-Job) until completion and retrieve results if the full operation was successful.
The [Data Source](appendix.html#term-Data-Source) configuration therefore indicates to Weaver how to map a given data reference to a specific
instance or server where that data is expected to reside. This procedure effectively allows Weaver to deliver
applications close to the data which can be extremely more efficient (both in terms of time and quantity) than
pulling the data locally when [Data Source](appendix.html#term-Data-Source) become substantial. Furthermore, it allows [Data Source](appendix.html#term-Data-Source)
providers to define custom or private data retrieval mechanisms, where data cannot be exposed or offered externally,
but are still available for use when requested.
Details
[18](#id85)]
Configuration [HYBRID](appendix.html#term-HYBRID) applies here in cases where Weaver acts as an [EMS](appendix.html#term-EMS) for remote dispatch
of [Process](appendix.html#term-Process) execution based on applicable [File Reference Types](#file-ref-types).
See also
Specific details about configuration of [Data Source](appendix.html#term-Data-Source) are provided in the [Configuration of Data Sources](configuration.html#conf-data-sources) section.
See also
Details regarding [OpenSearch Data Source](#opensearch-data-source) are also relevant when resolving possible matches
of [Data Source](appendix.html#term-Data-Source) provider when the applicable [File Reference Types](#file-ref-types) are detected.

sklearn.covariancepartial_fit contract.
Where sklearn.covariance estimators are batch-only, every estimator here
updates one observation at a time and exposes covariance_,
correlation_, precision_ and location_. On top of
the estimators it adds a registry, river-style adapters for variables that enter and leave
a universe, a panel of assessors for judging an estimate, a recommender that
picks an estimator from observable data features, and the Schur pseudo-likelihood
— a one-parameter bridge between the full and block-diagonal Gaussian likelihoods.
pip install precise
numpy is the only required dependency (tested on numpy 1.26 and
2.x, Python 3.9–3.13). Optional extras: [pandas] (DataFrame output for
the keyed adapters), [research], [dev].
import numpy as np
from precise import EwaCovariance
est = EwaCovariance(r=0.05) # exponentially weighted, online
for y in stream_of_vectors(): # y is a 1-D array, one observation
est.partial_fit(y)
est.covariance_ # (d, d) ndarray, always symmetric PSD
est.correlation_ # unit-diagonal correlation
est.precision_ # inverse (when well-conditioned)
est.location_ # running mean
Every estimator follows the same contract, so a test harness (or your code) only needs
to look for .fit / .partial_fit. Discover them programmatically:
from precise import all_estimators, estimator_from_name
all_estimators() # list of estimator classes
estimator_from_name("LedoitWolfCovariance")
Fourteen truly-online estimators across families (no buffered recompute):
| Class | Family | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| EmpiricalCovariance | sample | Welford running covariance |
| DiagonalCovariance | sample | variances only |
| EwaCovariance | weighted | exponentially weighted |
| AdaptiveEwaCovariance | weighted | surprise-smoothed forgetting |
| LedoitWolfCovariance | shrinkage | online linear shrinkage |
| OASCovariance | shrinkage | oracle approximating shrinkage |
| ShrunkCovariance | shrinkage | fixed-intensity target |
| SchurCovariance | shrinkage | cross-block coupling damping (linear/geodesic) |
| PartialMomentsCovariance | semi | downside / semi-covariance |
| HuberCovariance | robust | online Huber M-estimator |
| TylerCovariance | robust | recursive Tyler M-estimator |
| GeodesicEwaCovariance | geometric | affine-invariant SPD geodesic step |
| DCCCovariance | dynamic | decoupled vol & correlation |
| FactorCovariance | factor | low-rank + diagonal, O(d·k)/step |
Finance rarely offers a fixed set of variables. The keyed adapters wrap any positional estimator into a river-style one over named variables that enter and leave:
from precise import keyed, EwaCovariance
est = keyed(EwaCovariance(r=0.05))
est.partial_fit({"AAPL": 0.01, "MSFT": -0.02}) # dict in, dict-of-dicts out
est.covariance_["AAPL"]["MSFT"]
FixedUniverse imputes missing keys;
DynamicUniverse handles staleness/longevity eviction and pairwise assembly
across changing key sets.
Because no estimator dominates every regime, precise treats
choosing and judging an estimate as first-class:
from precise import all_assessors, suggest
all_assessors() # LogLikelihood, BlockPseudoLikelihood,
# SchurLikelihood, SteinLoss, ... (higher = better)
suggest(X, top=3) # recommend estimator classes from data features
suggest maps observable, truth-free features (p/n, effective rank,
sphericity, condition number, off-diagonal mass, excess kurtosis) to an estimator via a
frozen, numpy-only decision tree.
The full Gaussian likelihood factorizes exactly, through Schur complements, into
block-conditional terms. A single coupling-strength parameter
γ ∈ [0,1] damps that conditioning, giving the Schur
pseudo-likelihood ℓγ: γ=1 is the full
likelihood (fragile in high dimensions), γ=0 is the block-diagonal /
composite likelihood (robust), and the interior is the bridge they lack. The same
γ damping of the same Schur complement is Schur complementary portfolio
allocation — interpolating hierarchical risk parity and minimum variance.
For the estimator/predictive use, the optimal trust has a closed form — the reliability of the coupling (a Wiener / James–Stein shrinkage):
γ* = (n−2) ρ² / [ (n−2) ρ² + (1 − ρ²) ] (ρ² = block coupling, the conditional R²)
rising to 1 as the sample size or coupling grows, and to 0 as the coupling becomes
noise. See the working paper,
[Schur Covariance Evaluation: A Principled
Pseudo-Likelihood in High Dimensions](papers/schur-likelihood/) ([read online](papers/schur-likelihood/) ·
[PDF](https://github.com/microprediction/precise/blob/main/papers/schur_likelihood_paper.pdf)).
pip install preciseOnline estimation does a constant amount of work per observation instead of recomputing
over a growing window — orders of magnitude less compute, and energy, over a long stream.
As a bonus, the partial_fit contract makes lookahead bias structurally hard: an
estimator only ever sees data up to the current observation, never the future. Drop the
precise skill into your own agent:
Read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microprediction/precise/main/SKILL.md
and create a project skill from it.
